senses.label: THE LITERATURE CANNOT BE RE-EXAMINED, BECAUSE THE DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE WAS NEVER PUBLISHED: place-coding studies analyse spike timing and only rarely show waveforms, so it is unknown whether they counted these units as place cells
senses.evidence: Because studies of hippocampal place coding typically analyze spike timing but spike waveforms are only rarely shown, it is unknown whether previous studies considered Punits and BIPs as place cells.

senses.label: THREE RIVAL ACCOUNTS NAMED IN ADVANCE: axonal forward propagation, dendritic backpropagation, and return currents - with the compartmental origin declared NOT ESTABLISHED
senses.head: THREE RIVAL ACCOUNTS NAMED IN ADVANCE: axonal forward propagation, dendritic backpropagation, and return currents
senses.gloss: with the compartmental origin declared NOT ESTABLISHED
senses.evidence: Taken together, the experimental findings and computational models support three hypotheses for the source of non-negative extracellular potentials during action potentials: axonal forward propagation, dendritic backpropagation, and return currents. Thus, the compartmental origin of non-negative extracellular waveforms is not established.

senses.label: AND EACH IS SEPARATED BY A DIFFERENT MEASURABLE PROPERTY: axonal potentials narrower because of channel density, backpropagating ones wider, return currents narrow and synchronous or slightly early
senses.evidence: Sodium spikes generated at the axon initial segment (AIS) actively propagate forward along the axon and backwards into the soma and dendrites 37 , 38 . Therefore, in extracellular recordings near the soma, potentials generated by axons and backpropagation into the dendrites are expected to exhibit sub-millisecond time lags with respect to somatic spikes due to conductance time. Axonal potentials are expected to be narrower than the somatic spikes due to higher density of voltage-gated potassium (Kv1) channels in the AIS 39 , whereas backpropagating spikes are expected to be wider due to lower dendritic density of KA channels 40 . On the other hand, return currents in the proximal dendrites are expected to balance AIS spikes. Charge movement time, AIS-to-soma propagation delay, and the somatic charging add up to several dozens of μs, therefore return currents are expected to be narrow and occur in synchrony with or slightly before the somatic spikes.

senses.label: the backpropagation account is then killed by width - the observed spikes are NARROWER than the somatic ones, where backpropagating spikes are wider
senses.head: the backpropagation account is then killed by width
senses.gloss: the observed spikes are NARROWER than the somatic ones, where backpropagating spikes are wider
senses.evidence: It was suggested that P-spikes in vitro 17 and B-spikes in vivo 34 , 35 correspond to active backpropagation of somatic spikes into dendrites 43 . Previously-reported non-negative spikes were seen far from the somatic potentials 36 , whereas most of our P- and B-spikes were in close proximity to the N-spikes. Backpropagating spikes are wider than somatic signals 40 , 43 . Because the P- and B-spikes in the present dataset are narrower than N-spikes, the non-negative spikes are unlikely to be produced by backpropagation.

senses.label: and the dendritic account by order - the positive phase is in synchrony with the negative spike and the biphasic trough comes after it, which forward propagation from the dendrites cannot give
senses.head: and the dendritic account by order
senses.gloss: the positive phase is in synchrony with the negative spike and the biphasic trough comes after it, which forward propagation from the dendrites cannot give
senses.evidence: Sodium spikes can be generated not only in the soma/AIS but also in the dendrites 57 – 59 . In vitro 18 , 31 and in silico 32 , 33 , B-spikes were suggested to be generated in the dendrites by forward propagation of dendritic sodium spikes. In MM units, P-spikes were in sync with N-spikes, and the trough of the B-spikes occurred after the N-spike trough. Therefore, it is unlikely that P- and B-spikes were created by forward propagation of dendritic sodium spikes. Dendrites can also generate calcium spikes 60 , 61 . In a dendritic calcium spike, P- and B-spikes are expected to appear before the somatic spike, but calcium spikes are much wider. Thus, the most likely compartmental counterparts of MM P- and B-spikes are dendritic return currents and axonal potentials.

senses.label: THREE ARTEFACTUAL EXPLANATIONS ELIMINATED TOO, EACH BY ITS OWN OBSERVATION: gap junctions would give two-sided cross-correlograms and these are unidirectional
senses.evidence: The short time lags of excitatory vINT-BIP pairs and the high-fidelity PYR-BIP transmission may suggest that B-spikes are generated by inter-neuronal gap junctions 66 – 68 . However, gap junction prevalence among neocortical PYRs is low 68 , inconsistent with the observation of neocortical MM PYRs with non-negative spikes. Moreover, neurons coupled by gap junctions typically yield CCHs with two-sided peaks 67 , 69 , whereas the CCHs of the excitatory vINT-BIP and PYR-BIP pairs are unidirectional. Therefore, it is unlikely that “excitatory” connections to BIP were caused by gap junctions.

senses.label: juxtacellular contact is ruled out by the electrode being the same size as the soma AND by the waveforms appearing alongside other units on the same electrode
senses.evidence: A possible source of SM Punits is sporadic juxtacellular recording, established by electrode adhesion to the membrane 70 . However, the sizes of the electrodes employed (10 × 15 μm) and the diameter of a PYR soma (10–15 μm 71 ) are similar. Furthermore, SM Punit waveforms were recorded together with waveforms of other units by the same electrode. Thus, non-negative extracellular waveforms are unlikely to be due to juxtacellular recordings.

senses.label: and potassium spikes by sharpness - previously reported ones are slow, these are much sharper
senses.head: and potassium spikes by sharpness
senses.gloss: previously reported ones are slow, these are much sharper
senses.evidence: In principle, P-spikes can be generated by somatic potassium action potentials. Potassium spikes were previously observed as slow “hyperpolarizing” responses in invertebrate muscles 72 , 73 , and may occur in neurons when extracellular potassium concentrations are very high or when potassium channels are inactivated 74 . However, the presently-reported P-spikes occur together with N-spikes and are much sharper than previously-reported potassium spikes.

senses.label: THE GEOMETRY IS THE DISCRIMINATOR: the two regions have OPPOSITE axo-dendritic orientation, which is what makes the comparison between them informative
senses.evidence: The opposite axo-dendritic orientation of pyramidal cells in neocortex and CA1 makes the comparison between the two regions informative. Furthermore, the laminar organization of CA1, the distinct place coding in pyramidal cells in CA1 and in CA3 41 , and the local generation of high frequency ripples, allow differentiating between local and non-local generation of non-negative spikes.

senses.label: and the relative orientation of the array and the axo-dendritic axis is shown by modeling to change the recorded waveform, so the apparent prevalence is partly a fact about the probe
senses.evidence: Indeed, modeling 77 showed that for a polarized multi-compartmental neuron, the relative orientation of the electrode array and the axo-dendritic axis impacts the recorded waveforms. It is a-priori possible that some of the CA1 Punits and BIPs represent non-somatic (e.g., axonal) compartments of CA3 neurons projecting to CA1. Place coding in CA3 PYRs includes lower fraction of place cells, larger place fields, higher spatial information, and lower phase precession prevalence 41 . However, the prevalence and properties of place coding by SM CA1 BIPs and Punits were not consistently different from CA1 PYR place coding. Thus, the properties of Punits and BIPs recorded in CA1 are inconsistent with CA3 place coding.

senses.label: A RIVAL SOURCE ELIMINATED BY A PROPERTY PROFILE: CA3 place coding has a lower fraction of place cells, larger fields, higher spatial information and less phase precession, and these units do not match it
senses.evidence: Indeed, modeling 77 showed that for a polarized multi-compartmental neuron, the relative orientation of the electrode array and the axo-dendritic axis impacts the recorded waveforms. It is a-priori possible that some of the CA1 Punits and BIPs represent non-somatic (e.g., axonal) compartments of CA3 neurons projecting to CA1. Place coding in CA3 PYRs includes lower fraction of place cells, larger place fields, higher spatial information, and lower phase precession prevalence 41 . However, the prevalence and properties of place coding by SM CA1 BIPs and Punits were not consistently different from CA1 PYR place coding. Thus, the properties of Punits and BIPs recorded in CA1 are inconsistent with CA3 place coding.

senses.label: THE FINDINGS ARE DECLARED CORRELATIVE AND THE CAUSAL TEST IS SPECIFIED: block axonal sodium channels and the biphasic units should lose their positive phase, block proximal dendritic ones and the two peaks should move apart
senses.evidence: Punits and BIPs were most consistent with return currents and axonal spikes, but all findings were correlative and we did not demonstrate causality. A causal link may be achieved using compartmental blockade. During recordings from the CA1 feedforward network, a specific blocker for axonal sodium channels (NaV1.2 81 , 82 ) may be applied locally. We predict that MM PYRs with B-spikes to be recorded before and during the blockade will turn to SM PYRs with only N-spikes during the blockade, and that BIPs will disappear. Alternatively, if sodium channels in proximal dendrites are blocked (NaV1.6 83 ), the N-spike to P-spike distance is expected to increase in MM PYRs with P-spikes.

senses.label: ONE QUANTITY, FIVE NAMES, AND THE PAPER LISTS THEM WITH CITATIONS: PREVIOUS STUDIES HAVE REFERRED TO THE STG USING VARIOUS OTHER NAMES: “EFFECTIVENESS”, “ASYNCHRONOUS GAIN”, “SYNAPTIC EFFICACY”, AND “SPIKE TRANSMISSION PROBABILITY”. A `renamed-across-fields` edge that the corpus usually has to infer, printed in the source
senses.evidence: Previous studies have referred to the STG using various other names: “effectiveness” 33 , “asynchronous gain” 34 , “synaptic efficacy” 11 , and “spike transmission probability”

senses.label: THREE PUBLISHED ESTIMATORS OF THE SAME QUANTITY, ON THE SAME DATA, WITH A KNOWN ANSWER, DISAGREE FROM 58% TO 133%: THE TAILS PREDICTOR OVERESTIMATED THE rSTG (133%), AND THE JITTER AND MEDIAN PREDICTORS UNDERESTIMATED IT (JITTER: 58%; MEDIAN FILTERING: 70%). Not noise - the sign of the error is a property of the estimator
senses.head: THREE PUBLISHED ESTIMATORS OF THE SAME QUANTITY, ON THE SAME DATA, WITH A KNOWN ANSWER, DISAGREE FROM 58% TO 133%: THE TAILS PREDICTOR OVERESTIMATED THE rSTG (133%), AND THE JITTER AND MEDIAN PREDICTORS UNDERESTIMATED IT (JITTER: 58%; MEDIAN FILTERING: 70%). Not noise
senses.gloss: the sign of the error is a property of the estimator
senses.evidence: The tails predictor overestimated the rSTG (eSTG = 0.053, 133%; Fig. 3d ), and the jitter and median predictors underestimated the rSTG (jitter: 0.023, 58%; median filtering: 0.028, 70%). Thus, when burst spiking activity is present, the tails, jitter, and median methods fail to produce an accurate eSTG.

senses.label: AND THE NUMBER MOVES WITH A PROPERTY THAT IS NOT THE CONNECTION: ALTHOUGH E-TO-I CONNECTION STRENGTHS WERE THE SAME FOR ALL PAIRS, MEDIAN FILTERING WITHOUT DECONVOLUTION YIELDED eSTGs WHICH WERE HIGHLY AFFECTED BY THE BF. Identical ground truth, and the measurement varies with how the presynaptic cell happens to fire
senses.evidence: Although E-to-I connection strengths were the same for all pairs, median filtering without deconvolution yielded eSTGs which were highly affected by the BF ( ρ = −0.68, p < 0.001, permutation test; Fig. 5e ). In contrast, median filtering with deconvolution produced eSTGs that were not correlated with burstiness

senses.label: stated by the authors as the general form: EVEN WHEN CONNECTIONS HAVE FIXED STRENGTHS, THE eSTGs DEPEND ON BURST SPIKING ACTIVITY
senses.evidence: Thus, even when connections have fixed strengths, the eSTGs depend on burst spiking activity. However, dependency is minimized using deconvolution.

senses.label: THE FIELD'S SHARED ASSUMPTION, WRITTEN OUT: AN UNDERLYING ASSUMPTION IN THESE APPROACHES IS THAT WHILE DIRECT CONNECTIONS EXHIBIT FAST TRANSIENTS IN THE CCH, INDIRECT SOURCES PRODUCE SLOWER FLUCTUATIONS - the whole timescale-separation family rests on it
senses.head: THE FIELD'S SHARED ASSUMPTION, WRITTEN OUT: AN UNDERLYING ASSUMPTION IN THESE APPROACHES IS THAT WHILE DIRECT CONNECTIONS EXHIBIT FAST TRANSIENTS IN THE CCH, INDIRECT SOURCES PRODUCE SLOWER FLUCTUATIONS
senses.gloss: the whole timescale-separation family rests on it
senses.evidence: An underlying assumption in these approaches is that while direct connections exhibit fast transients in the CCH, indirect sources produce slower fluctuations. Based on this assumption, timescale separation can be used to detect and estimate synaptic connectivity, differentiating between fast transients (which are presumably due to direct connectivity), and slower fluctuations (which are presumably due to other sources).

senses.label: and then broken by a case it does not cover: WHEN ONE OF TWO CONNECTED NEURONS EXHIBITS HIGH-FREQUENCY PERIODICITY OR BURST SPIKING, FAST FEATURES APPEAR IN THE CCH, and THESE FEATURES CANNOT BE DIFFERENTIATED FROM TRANSMITTED SPIKES BY TIMESCALE SEPARATION
senses.evidence: When one of two connected neurons exhibits high-frequency periodicity or burst spiking, fast features appear in the CCH 22 , 23 . These features cannot be differentiated from transmitted spikes by timescale separation. Thus, even when timescale separation methods are used, transmitted spikes cannot be fully differentiated from non-transmission patterns such as burst spiking activity.

senses.label: TWO OF THE FIVE METHODS REPORT IN UNITS THE GROUND TRUTH DOES NOT HAVE: THE TAILS, JITTER, AND MEDIAN FILTERING METHODS YIELD ESTIMATES MEASURED AS GAIN, THE GLMCC AND CoNNECT METHODS PRODUCE ESTIMATES IN UNITS OF mV, and THE ESTIMATES YIELDED BY THE PSP-BASED METHODS CANNOT BE GAUGED DIRECTLY, SINCE NO GROUND TRUTH FOR PSP EXISTS IN THE POINT PROCESS SIMULATIONS
senses.evidence: While the tails, jitter, and median filtering methods yield estimates of effective connectivity measured as gain (STG; Fig. 1 ), the GLMCC and CoNNECT methods produce estimates in units of mV (PSP). The estimates yielded by the PSP-based methods cannot be gauged directly in the case of the synthetic CCH depicted in Fig. 3c , since no ground truth for PSP exists in the point process simulations.

senses.label: THE MEASUREMENT IS CORRELATIVE AND THE PAPER SAYS SO: MOST CCH APPLICATIONS EMPLOY SPONTANEOUS SPIKING, AND ARE THEREFORE CORRELATIVE MEASUREMENTS WHICH CANNOT DIFFERENTIATE CAUSAL TRANSMISSION FROM NON-CAUSAL SPIKE PATTERNS - every `causes` edge built on a CCH inherits this
senses.head: THE MEASUREMENT IS CORRELATIVE AND THE PAPER SAYS SO: MOST CCH APPLICATIONS EMPLOY SPONTANEOUS SPIKING, AND ARE THEREFORE CORRELATIVE MEASUREMENTS WHICH CANNOT DIFFERENTIATE CAUSAL TRANSMISSION FROM NON-CAUSAL SPIKE PATTERNS
senses.gloss: every `causes` edge built on a CCH inherits this
senses.evidence: However, most CCH applications employ spontaneous spiking, and are therefore correlative measurements which cannot differentiate causal transmission from non-causal spike patterns. For example, firing of two cells may be co-modulated by another source such as visual input or a third neuron, causing the two cells to fire in synchrony 12 . Thus, the CCH is influenced not only by spike transmission properties but also by co-modulation of the pre- and postsynaptic trains

senses.label: A QUANTITY THAT DOES NOT DETERMINE WHAT ITS NAME SUGGESTS: EPSP MAGNITUDE ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT FOR DETERMINING WHETHER A POSTSYNAPTIC NEURON WILL FIRE FOLLOWING A PRESYNAPTIC SPIKE, THEREBY ALLOWING INFORMATION TO PASS ON TO OTHER CELLS
senses.evidence: Thus, EPSP magnitude alone is insufficient for determining whether a postsynaptic neuron will fire following a presynaptic spike, thereby allowing information to pass on to other cells.

senses.label: and the missing variable is named and measured: WHILE EVEN RELATIVELY-LARGE EPSPs FAIL TO PRODUCE POSTSYNAPTIC SPIKES IN THE LACK OF MEMBRANE POTENTIAL VARIABILITY, WEAKER EPSPs (0.2-1 mV) COULD INDUCE CONSISTENT SPIKING WHEN NOISE WAS SUFFICIENTLY HIGH. The same synapse, opposite outcomes, decided by the background
senses.evidence: While even relatively-large EPSPs fail to produce postsynaptic spikes in the lack of membrane potential variability, weaker EPSPs (0.2–1 mV) could induce consistent spiking when noise was sufficiently high. Moreover, the uEPSP magnitude required to generate a fixed rSTG decreased monotonically with σ (Fig. 1b , bottom inset). Thus, EPSP magnitude alone does not suffice for estimating spike transmission.

senses.label: THE OBVIOUS DEFINITION OF THE GROUND TRUTH IS WRONG, AND THE PAPER DERIVES THE CORRECTION: SUCH COMPUTATION IS FLAWED SINCE THE ADDITION OF TRANSMITTED SPIKES OCCASIONALLY DECIMATES SPONTANEOUS (NOISE-INDUCED) SPIKES - THE EXACT rSTG IS OBTAINED BY MULTIPLYING THE NAIVE RATIO BY A CORRECTION FACTOR THAT SCALES THE FIRING RATE DIFFERENCE BY THE FRACTION OF NON-OCCUPIED BINS
senses.head: THE OBVIOUS DEFINITION OF THE GROUND TRUTH IS WRONG, AND THE PAPER DERIVES THE CORRECTION: SUCH COMPUTATION IS FLAWED SINCE THE ADDITION OF TRANSMITTED SPIKES OCCASIONALLY DECIMATES SPONTANEOUS (NOISE-INDUCED) SPIKES
senses.gloss: THE EXACT rSTG IS OBTAINED BY MULTIPLYING THE NAIVE RATIO BY A CORRECTION FACTOR THAT SCALES THE FIRING RATE DIFFERENCE BY THE FRACTION OF NON-OCCUPIED BINS
senses.evidence: However, such computation is flawed since the addition of transmitted spikes occasionally decimates spontaneous (noise-induced) spikes. In the case of a LIF model with an absolute refractory period ARP 2 and time step Δ t , the exact rSTG is obtained by multiplying the naive ratio by a correction factor that scales the firing rate difference by the fraction of non-occupied bins

senses.label: THE ASSUMPTION THE WHOLE PAPER RESTS ON, STATED WITH THE EVIDENCE AGAINST IT: THE UNDERLYING ASSUMPTION WAS THAT THE ACHs AND CONNECTIVITY STRENGTHS ARE FIXED OVER TIME - and SPIKE TRANSMISSION ESTIMATES DERIVED FROM THE CCH IN VIVO WERE DISTINCT WHEN CCHs WERE COMPUTED USING THE FIRST, SECOND, OR THIRD SPIKE IN A PRESYNAPTIC BURST
senses.head: THE ASSUMPTION THE WHOLE PAPER RESTS ON, STATED WITH THE EVIDENCE AGAINST IT: THE UNDERLYING ASSUMPTION WAS THAT THE ACHs AND CONNECTIVITY STRENGTHS ARE FIXED OVER TIME
senses.gloss: and SPIKE TRANSMISSION ESTIMATES DERIVED FROM THE CCH IN VIVO WERE DISTINCT WHEN CCHs WERE COMPUTED USING THE FIRST, SECOND, OR THIRD SPIKE IN A PRESYNAPTIC BURST
senses.evidence: Estimates of STG/PSP yielded by all methods employed (tails, jitter, median, GLMCC, and CoNNECT) were averaged over time and spike patterns. The underlying assumption was that the ACHs and connectivity strengths are fixed over time. However, previous studies have shown that the postsynaptic effect of a presynaptic spike may depend on the presynaptic inter-spike interval 3 , 10 , 11 and on other parameters 32 , 47 . In vitro work showed that synaptic transmission can exhibit short-term plasticity, where the EPSP magnitude in a postsynaptic neuron is modified according to the order and timing of presynaptic spikes 48 . In some cases, EPSP magnitude decreased over consecutive spikes, and in other cases consecutive spikes caused facilitation of EPSP magnitude 3 , 49 . Consistent with the in vitro work, spike transmission estimates derived from the CCH in vivo were distinct when CCHs were computed using the first, second, or third spike in a presynaptic burst 21 , 32 , 50 , 51 . Other in vivo studies used trial-averaging and time-resolved cross-correlation measures, showing that spike-to-spike correlations depend on the time lag relative to a stimulus or an action 32 , 47 , 52 . As is, the deconvolution approach presented here (as well as the timescale separation methods employed) does not take into account time-dependent changes in the auto-correlation (e.g., of bursting activity) and cannot estimate time-dependent changes of spike transmission.

senses.label: AN APPROXIMATION WITH ITS DOMAIN PRINTED: THE APPROXIMATION IS VALID AS LONG AS THE PRODUCT OF THE TWO STGs (I.E., THE LOOP GAIN) IS SMALL
senses.evidence: The approximation is valid as long as the product of the two STGs (i.e., the loop gain) is small.

senses.label: AND THE REAL DATA HAS NO GROUND TRUTH AT ALL: IN CONTRAST TO SIMULATIONS, rSTGs ARE OF COURSE UNKNOWN FOR THE REAL NEURONAL DATA - so the real-data claim is a consistency check against the simulations, not a measurement of accuracy
senses.head: AND THE REAL DATA HAS NO GROUND TRUTH AT ALL: IN CONTRAST TO SIMULATIONS, rSTGs ARE OF COURSE UNKNOWN FOR THE REAL NEURONAL DATA
senses.gloss: so the real-data claim is a consistency check against the simulations, not a measurement of accuracy
senses.evidence: In contrast to simulations, rSTGs are of course unknown for the real neuronal data. Therefore, we tested the contribution of deconvolution by measuring the eSTG ratio (without and with deconvolution) as a function of the burst index.

senses.label: a negative reported about the authors' own tool: WITH THE EXCEPTION OF CoNNECT, DECONVOLUTION REDUCED THE EFFECT OF BURSTING FOR ALL METHODS
senses.evidence: With the exception of CoNNECT, deconvolution reduced the effect of bursting for all methods

senses.label: THE METHOD WAS CHOSEN ON TWO CRITERIA AND ONE OF THEM IS SPEED: OF THE STG-BASED METHODS, MEDIAN FILTERING YIELDED THE BEST PERFORMANCE, and its runtime was THREE TO FOUR ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE FASTER THAN THE RUNTIME OF PSP-BASED METHODS
senses.evidence: To focus on the contribution of deconvolution, we chose to use a single timescale separation method from this point onward. Of the STG-based methods, median filtering yielded the best performance, with respect to both quantification (Fig. 4h ) and detection (Fig. 4t ). Run times were tested on synthetic spike trains with firing rates of 2 and 8 spk/s, recorded over 5 h. The median [IQR] runtime of median filtering was 0.65 [0.64 0.67] ms, three to four orders of magnitude faster than the runtime of PSP-based methods (GLMCC: 3.72 [2.88 4.55] s; CoNNECT: 1.62 [1.54 1.69] s). These runtimes and performance made median filtering our method of choice for evaluating the contribution of deconvolution in biophysical simulations

senses.label: the improvement, in the units of the thing being estimated: DECONVOLUTION REDUCED THE MSE FOR ALL STG-BASED METHODS, approximately TWO-FOLD
senses.evidence: We found that deconvolution reduced the MSE for all STG-based methods ( p < 0.001; Wilcoxon’s paired signed-rank test; Fig. 4h ). Of the three STG-based methods, median filtering with deconvolution had the lowest MSE (1.27 × 10 −5 ). Median without deconvolution and jitter with deconvolution had the second and third lowest MSEs, respectively (median: 2.73 × 10 −5 ; jitter with deconvolution: 3.48 × 10 −5 ; jitter: 5.34 × 10 −5 ). Thus, deconvolution reduced the errors approximately two-fold.

senses.label: and the claim generalizes beyond the case tested: WHILE BURSTING IS A RELATIVELY COMMON DEVIATION FROM POISSON SPIKING IN REAL SPIKE TRAINS, OTHER DEVIATIONS ARE CLEARLY POSSIBLE - WHEN INDIVIDUAL NEURONS EXHIBIT PHASE LOCKING TO FIELD OSCILLATIONS, THE ACH MAY EXHIBIT PERIODICITY, and THE CCH BETWEEN CONNECTED NEURONS WILL BE AFFECTED BY ACH PERIODICITY
senses.head: and the claim generalizes beyond the case tested: WHILE BURSTING IS A RELATIVELY COMMON DEVIATION FROM POISSON SPIKING IN REAL SPIKE TRAINS, OTHER DEVIATIONS ARE CLEARLY POSSIBLE
senses.gloss: WHEN INDIVIDUAL NEURONS EXHIBIT PHASE LOCKING TO FIELD OSCILLATIONS, THE ACH MAY EXHIBIT PERIODICITY, and THE CCH BETWEEN CONNECTED NEURONS WILL BE AFFECTED BY ACH PERIODICITY
senses.evidence: We showed that deconvolution improves connectivity estimates for bursting activity, but deconvolution can remove other effects of second-order spike train statistics on the CCH. While bursting is a relatively common deviation from Poisson spiking in real spike trains, other deviations are clearly possible. For instance, in some brain regions, strong periodicity is encountered, for instance at the ripple 53 or gamma 54 range. When individual neurons exhibit phase locking to field oscillations, the ACH may exhibit periodicity 54 , 55 . Then, the CCH between connected neurons will be affected by ACH periodicity. Deconvolution can be used to differentiate between the effect of transmitted spikes and the firing patterns of the presynaptic neuron. Thus, deconvolution can minimize the distortion of connectivity estimates and improve the analysis of slower CCH features.

senses.label: the real-data result stated as direction, not size: DECONVOLUTION-BASED eSTGs WERE CONSISTENTLY HIGHER THAN eSTGs WITHOUT DECONVOLUTION (MEDIANS: 0.019 AND 0.017)
senses.evidence: For the analysis pairs only, deconvolution-based eSTGs were consistently higher than eSTGs without deconvolution (medians: 0.019 and 0.017, respectively; p < 0.001, Wilcoxon’s paired signed-rank; Fig. 6d ).

senses.label: A DEFINITION THAT CARRIES A SIGN CONVENTION: THE eSTG IS THE AREA UNDER THE STC PEAK IN A TEMPORAL REGION OF INTEREST, DIVIDED BY THE NUMBER OF PRESYNAPTIC SPIKES - and FOR AN STC BELOW BASELINE, THE STG IS A NEGATIVE QUANTITY
senses.head: A DEFINITION THAT CARRIES A SIGN CONVENTION: THE eSTG IS THE AREA UNDER THE STC PEAK IN A TEMPORAL REGION OF INTEREST, DIVIDED BY THE NUMBER OF PRESYNAPTIC SPIKES
senses.gloss: and FOR AN STC BELOW BASELINE, THE STG IS A NEGATIVE QUANTITY
senses.evidence: We then defined the estimated STG (eSTG) as the area under the STC peak in a temporal region of interest (ROI; defined here as 0 < τ ≤ 5 ms 32 ; Fig. 1c , gray bins), divided by the number of presynaptic spikes. For an STC below baseline, the STG is a negative quantity.

senses.label: PRIMING MEASURED IN FORCE. The dependent variable is how hard somebody squeezes a handgrip, with pupil dilation and motor-evoked potentials alongside it. Nearly every other record in this corpus measures priming as speed, accuracy, choice or judgement; this one measures a physical output and a physiological state, which means the effect has to survive translation into the motor system rather than staying in a decision
senses.evidence: The priming effect was measured behaviourally by handgrip force and reaction time to the grip cue after the priming was complete. Physiologically, the effects were measured by pupil dilation and motor-evoked potentials

senses.label: BOTH CONDITIONS WORK - AND THE PAPER REFUSES THE EQUIVALENCE READING, WHICH IS THE ROW THAT MATTERS. `Therefore, it is clear that both subliminal and supraliminal goal-priming with positive words INCREASED THE VARIABLES, while WE SHOULD BE CAUTIOUS ABOUT THE INTERPRETATION THAT THE DEGREE OF INCREASE WAS IDENTICAL between the two conditions.` The effect survives visibility; the SAMENESS of the effect is explicitly not claimed, and the discussion offers the opposite possibility too - that supraliminal presentation `might cause greater enhancement`. A paper declining an equivalence its own abstract could have been read as asserting
senses.head: BOTH CONDITIONS WORK
senses.gloss: AND THE PAPER REFUSES THE EQUIVALENCE READING, WHICH IS THE ROW THAT MATTERS. `Therefore, it is clear that both subliminal and supraliminal goal-priming with positive words INCREASED THE VARIABLES, while WE SHOULD BE CAUTIOUS ABOUT THE INTERPRETATION THAT THE DEGREE OF INCREASE WAS IDENTICAL between the two conditions.` The effect survives visibility; the SAMENESS of the effect is explicitly not claimed, and the discussion offers the opposite possibility too - that supraliminal presentation `might cause greater enhancement`. A paper declining an equivalence its own abstract could have been read as asserting
senses.evidence: Therefore, it is clear that both subliminal and supraliminal goal-priming with positive words increased the variables, while we should be cautious about the interpretation that the degree of increase was identical between the two conditions

senses.label: THE AWARENESS CHECK IS THE OBJECTIVE KIND, AND IT CARRIES ITS NUMBER: `Response accuracy was 50.15% +/- 6.23%, indicating that their judgements did not differ from chance, and that they could not see the priming words.` This is the zero-sensitivity criterion that Schmidt2011 argues should be retired because it presupposes an exhaustive awareness measure (Q-756), and the design Van-den-Bussche2013 calls confounded because masking changes strength as well as visibility (Q-753). The corpus now holds the criterion, its critique and a study using it
senses.evidence: Response accuracy was 50.15% ± 6.23%, indicating that their judgements did not differ from chance, and that they could not see the priming words

senses.label: AND ONE ASYMMETRY SURVIVES THE EQUIVALENCE: the supraliminal participants `did not experience any SUBJECTIVE DIFFERENCE IN EFFORT immediately after the motor action AS PARTICIPANTS IN THE SUBLIMINAL GROUP DID`. Force, reaction time, MEPs and pupil dilation all move alike across the awareness boundary - and the felt effort does not. A dissociation reported inside a paper whose headline is an equivalence, and the kind of detail a summary of the abstract would lose
senses.head: AND ONE ASYMMETRY SURVIVES THE EQUIVALENCE: the supraliminal participants `did not experience any SUBJECTIVE DIFFERENCE IN EFFORT immediately after the motor action AS PARTICIPANTS IN THE SUBLIMINAL GROUP DID`. Force, reaction time, MEPs and pupil dilation all move alike across the awareness boundary
senses.gloss: and the felt effort does not. A dissociation reported inside a paper whose headline is an equivalence, and the kind of detail a summary of the abstract would lose
senses.evidence: Meanwhile, they did not experience any subjective difference in effort immediately after the motor action as participants in the subliminal group did. This suggests that the enhancing effect of supraliminal goal priming with rewards in physical resources was automatic. At the same time, we must keep in mind that memory-based self-report (such as the CR-10 scale) is not the most sensitive or powerful measure of actual awareness during past actions 30 . Therefore, based on the proposed mechanism for unconscious goal pursuit

senses.label: integration - as a single leaky accumulator with one time constant, under which more sound always means better performance
senses.head: integration
senses.gloss: as a single leaky accumulator with one time constant, under which more sound always means better performance
senses.evidence: Previous models of temporal integration typically assume leaky integration with a time constant of hundreds of milliseconds, based on studies such as loudness summation 15 , 16 , signal detection in noise 17 , 18 , and temporal integration at threshold 13 , 19 , 20 , 21 , 22 , in which listeners’ performance increases continuously with sound duration and typically achieves a plateau above 200 ms.

senses.label: integration - as fast discrete sampling then concatenation, where the long scale is assembled from short samples
senses.head: integration
senses.gloss: as fast discrete sampling then concatenation, where the long scale is assembled from short samples
senses.evidence: The multiple-looks model suggests that temporal integration is a process of multiple timescales instead of one, but the longer timescale is assembled on the basis of concatenated short samples.

senses.label: integration - as two independent concurrent windows, where the long scale is not built from the short one and each does its own job
senses.head: integration
senses.gloss: as two independent concurrent windows, where the long scale is not built from the short one and each does its own job
senses.evidence: In contrast, the 2TWI model suggests that increased stimulus length may not necessarily increase performance, because representation and processing of local details might function best only at a time range of tens of milliseconds

senses.label: THE SIMPLEST HYPOTHESIS, STATED IN ORDER TO BE FALSIFIED: temporal modulations are encoded IN AN EQUIVALENT MANNER within a reasonable intermediate range - and the finding is that the system tracks at theta and gamma BUT, CONTRARY TO EXPECTATION, NOT AT ALPHA
senses.head: THE SIMPLEST HYPOTHESIS, STATED IN ORDER TO BE FALSIFIED: temporal modulations are encoded IN AN EQUIVALENT MANNER within a reasonable intermediate range
senses.gloss: and the finding is that the system tracks at theta and gamma BUT, CONTRARY TO EXPECTATION, NOT AT ALPHA
senses.evidence: Natural sounds convey perceptually relevant information over multiple timescales, and the necessary extraction of multi-timescale information requires the auditory system to work over distinct ranges. The simplest hypothesis suggests that temporal modulations are encoded in an equivalent manner within a reasonable intermediate range. We show that the human auditory system selectively and preferentially tracks acoustic dynamics concurrently at 2 timescales corresponding to the neurophysiological theta band (4–7 Hz) and gamma band ranges (31–45 Hz) but, contrary to expectation, not at the timescale corresponding to alpha (8–12 Hz), which has also been found to be related to auditory perception.

senses.label: THE HEADLINE IS A NEGATIVE RESULT: CRUCIALLY, NO ROBUST PHASE COHERENCE WAS FOUND IN THE ALPHA AND BETA BANDS - and this nonuniform pattern DOES NOT SUPPORT the simplest hypothesis of comparable neural tracking for all rates
senses.head: THE HEADLINE IS A NEGATIVE RESULT: CRUCIALLY, NO ROBUST PHASE COHERENCE WAS FOUND IN THE ALPHA AND BETA BANDS
senses.gloss: and this nonuniform pattern DOES NOT SUPPORT the simplest hypothesis of comparable neural tracking for all rates
senses.evidence: Crucially, no robust phase coherence was found in the alpha and beta bands. This nonuniform phase-response pattern across temporal regimes does not support the simplest hypothesis of comparable neural tracking for all stimulus modulation rates.

senses.label: and the null is about the band the field had every reason to expect: IT IS REASONABLE TO HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE ALPHA BAND IS FUNDAMENTAL TO AUDITORY PERCEPTION, AS DEMONSTRATED IN A RANGE OF STUDIES - attention, working memory, listening effort, speech intelligibility
senses.head: and the null is about the band the field had every reason to expect: IT IS REASONABLE TO HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE ALPHA BAND IS FUNDAMENTAL TO AUDITORY PERCEPTION, AS DEMONSTRATED IN A RANGE OF STUDIES
senses.gloss: attention, working memory, listening effort, speech intelligibility
senses.evidence: It is reasonable to hypothesize that the alpha band is fundamental to auditory perception, as demonstrated in a range of studies, but the timing (i.e., its intermediate position between lower theta and higher gamma activity) also invites the conjecture that alpha range activity reflects aspects of auditory processing on a timescale of approximately 100 ms. Here, we investigate directly the most straightforward hypothesis: does alpha band activity reflect the processing of acoustic information in a manner parallel to lower and higher neural frequencies?

senses.label: with the same null reached by a second, independent measure: NO SIGNIFICANT MAIN EFFECTS of the phase sound type were found for mutual information computed using the cochlear-scaled correlation of alpha sounds
senses.evidence: Importantly, no significant main effects of the phase sound type were found for mutual information computed using the cochlear-scaled correlation of α sounds.

senses.label: and a third: the alpha band DID NOT CONTRIBUTE SIGNIFICANTLY TO DECODING ANY STIMULI, while the beta band DETERIORATED decoding of gamma sounds
senses.evidence: The beta band deteriorated decoding of γ sounds ( t (14) = −4.66, p = 0.002, d = 1.20). Crucially, the alpha band did not contribute significantly to decoding any stimuli.

senses.label: A BAND WIDER THAN THE EFFECT IT IS MEANT TO MEASURE: the gamma coherence is real but comes out NOT SIGNIFICANT because it PEAKS WITHIN A NARROW FREQUENCY RANGE CENTERED AROUND 37 Hz, and AVERAGING FROM 30 TO 45 Hz DECREASES THE MEAN - the analysis window, not the brain, decides the verdict
senses.head: A BAND WIDER THAN THE EFFECT IT IS MEANT TO MEASURE: the gamma coherence is real but comes out NOT SIGNIFICANT because it PEAKS WITHIN A NARROW FREQUENCY RANGE CENTERED AROUND 37 Hz, and AVERAGING FROM 30 TO 45 Hz DECREASES THE MEAN
senses.gloss: the analysis window, not the brain, decides the verdict
senses.evidence: zITC of γ sounds in the gamma band is not significant ( t (14) = −0.15, p = 1.00, d = −0.03), likely because robust phase coherence peaks within a narrow frequency range centered around 37 Hz, as shown in the spectrum of zITC in Fig 1a . Averaging zITC of γ sound from 30 to 45 Hz decreases the mean of zITC in the gamma band.

senses.label: A CLAIM THAT IS NULL AND SIGNIFICANT DEPENDING ON ONE EXCLUSION, WITH BOTH NUMBERS PRINTED: before correction the gamma band shows a contribution at p = 0.057, and AFTER REMOVING 1 SUBJECT who showed abnormal decoding performance it is significant after FDR correction
senses.evidence: Before adjusted FDR correction, the gamma band shows a contribution to decoding γ sounds ( t (14) = 2.07, p = 0.057, d = 0.53). After removing 1 subject who showed abnormal decoding performance, we found that the gamma band significantly contributes to decoding γ sounds after FDR correction

senses.label: THE DISAMBIGUATION LIVES IN THE TYPOGRAPHY: in one sentence the Greek letter names the STIMULUS and the spelled-out word names the SIGNIFICANCE LEVEL - the alpha and gamma sounds evoked coherence above 1.64, THE CRITICAL Z-SCORE EQUIVALENT TO AN ALPHA LEVEL OF 0.05. Alphabet, not wording, carries the distinction, and alphabet is the first thing text extraction destroys
senses.head: THE DISAMBIGUATION LIVES IN THE TYPOGRAPHY: in one sentence the Greek letter names the STIMULUS and the spelled-out word names the SIGNIFICANCE LEVEL
senses.gloss: the alpha and gamma sounds evoked coherence above 1.64, THE CRITICAL Z-SCORE EQUIVALENT TO AN ALPHA LEVEL OF 0.05. Alphabet, not wording, carries the distinction, and alphabet is the first thing text extraction destroys
senses.evidence: However, the α and γ sounds also evoked robust phase coherence at a frequency range below 8 Hz, in which zITC of the group means for α and γ sounds are above 1.64—the critical z -score equivalent to an alpha level of 0.05 (1-tailed, Bonferroni corrected).

senses.label: AND THE STIMULUS IS NAMED AFTER THE BRAIN: we refer to the stimulus type with a modulation rate in theta band range AS A THETA SOUND, and likewise for alpha and gamma - so every result sentence carries the same word for the sound and for the neural band that may or may not track it
senses.head: AND THE STIMULUS IS NAMED AFTER THE BRAIN: we refer to the stimulus type with a modulation rate in theta band range AS A THETA SOUND, and likewise for alpha and gamma
senses.gloss: so every result sentence carries the same word for the sound and for the neural band that may or may not track it
senses.evidence: We refer to the stimulus type with a modulation rate in theta band range (4–7 Hz) as a theta (θ) sound, the stimulus type with modulation rate in the alpha band range (8–12 Hz) as an alpha ( α ) sound, and the stimulus type with modulation rate in the gamma band range (30–45 Hz) as a gamma (γ) sound.

senses.label: with the band edges moving between sections: the stimuli were aligned to theta (4-7 Hz), ALPHA/LOW BETA (8-15 Hz) and low gamma (30-45 Hz), while the analysis bands are alpha (8-12 Hz) and gamma (31-45 Hz) - the alpha sound's own range is written twice with different edges
senses.head: with the band edges moving between sections: the stimuli were aligned to theta (4-7 Hz), ALPHA/LOW BETA (8-15 Hz) and low gamma (30-45 Hz), while the analysis bands are alpha (8-12 Hz) and gamma (31-45 Hz)
senses.gloss: the alpha sound's own range is written twice with different edges
senses.evidence: The distribution of the segment durations of the stimuli aligned with the range of periods typical of theta (4–7 Hz), alpha/low beta (8–15 Hz), and low gamma (30–45 Hz) band neural oscillations. We refer to the stimulus type with mean segment duration of 190 ms as a theta ( θ ) sound, the stimulus type with mean segment duration of 100 ms as an alpha ( α ) sound, and the stimulus type with mean segment duration of 27 ms as a gamma ( γ ) sound.

senses.label: and the analysis bands stated exactly, which is what makes the mismatch visible at all: theta (4-7 Hz), alpha (8-12 Hz), beta (13-30 Hz), and gamma (31-45 Hz)
senses.evidence: The ITC and power data were averaged from 0.3 s to 1.8 s poststimulus onset to minimize the effects of stimulus-evoked onsets and offsets and within 4 frequency bands: theta (4–7 Hz), alpha (8–12 Hz), beta (13–30 Hz), and gamma (31–45 Hz).

senses.label: ENTRAINMENT IS NOT TRACKING, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO BEFORE MEASURING ANYTHING: cortical oscillations entrained by stimuli of corresponding frequencies ARE NOT SUFFICIENT to demonstrate the importance of a band, because the entrainment could simply reflect A MODULATION-FREQUENCY FOLLOWING RESPONSE WHICH MAY HAVE LITTLE TO DO WITH the system actively processing acoustic information
senses.evidence: Although these findings demonstrate dominant auditory responses in the low frequency range (delta-theta and alpha) and the gamma band, the cortical oscillations entrained by stimuli of corresponding frequencies of the regular modulation are not sufficient to demonstrate the importance of theta, alpha, and gamma bands in auditory processing, because the entrainment could simply reflect a modulation-frequency following response which may have little to do with the auditory system actively processing acoustic information in the theta and gamma bands.

senses.label: which is exactly what the mutual information analysis is for - the coherence is INDEED CAUSED BY TRACKING SPECIFIC ACOUSTIC STRUCTURES, RATHER THAN SIMPLY BEING EVOKED BY GENERIC ACOUSTIC STIMULI
senses.head: which is exactly what the mutual information analysis is for
senses.gloss: the coherence is INDEED CAUSED BY TRACKING SPECIFIC ACOUSTIC STRUCTURES, RATHER THAN SIMPLY BEING EVOKED BY GENERIC ACOUSTIC STIMULI
senses.evidence: The results of the mutual information analyses demonstrate that phase patterns in the theta and gamma bands track the temporal structure of the stimuli, as quantified by the cochlear-scaled correlation. The robust phase coherence observed in the theta band for θ sounds and that in the gamma band for γ sounds is indeed caused by tracking specific acoustic structures, rather than simply being evoked by generic acoustic stimuli.

senses.label: and the one place the two come apart: gamma sounds evoke robust coherence IN THE THETA BAND with NO specialized tracking there, which is read as the theta band CHUNKING rather than coding - a perceptual unit on a timescale of approximately 200 ms
senses.head: and the one place the two come apart: gamma sounds evoke robust coherence IN THE THETA BAND with NO specialized tracking there, which is read as the theta band CHUNKING rather than coding
senses.gloss: a perceptual unit on a timescale of approximately 200 ms
senses.evidence: We did not find specialized tracking for γ sounds in the theta band, although γ sounds evoked robust phase coherence in the theta band ( Fig 2a ). This could be because the theta band, instead of faithfully coding the temporal structure of γ sounds, chunks acoustic information and forms a perceptual unit on a timescale of approximately 200 ms (the theta band range).

senses.label: A SELECTION BIAS ADMITTED, WITH SELF-RESTRAINT AS THE REMEDY: participants may identify theta and gamma sounds more easily simply because those rates ARE LOCATED AT THE PERCEPTUAL EXTREMES in this design - the task is SUBOPTIMAL, and WE SCRUPULOUSLY REFRAIN FROM OVERINTERPRETING THESE DATA
senses.head: A SELECTION BIAS ADMITTED, WITH SELF-RESTRAINT AS THE REMEDY: participants may identify theta and gamma sounds more easily simply because those rates ARE LOCATED AT THE PERCEPTUAL EXTREMES in this design
senses.gloss: the task is SUBOPTIMAL, and WE SCRUPULOUSLY REFRAIN FROM OVERINTERPRETING THESE DATA
senses.evidence: However, the behavioral method used in the present study cannot circumvent a concern with a selection bias to different sounds, because participants may identify θ sounds and γ sounds more easily simply because the modulation rates of these 2 sounds are located at the perceptual extremes in this experimental design. We acknowledge that this behavioral task is suboptimal—and primarily employed to ensure attention during neurophysiological recording—so we scrupulously refrain from overinterpreting these data, beyond pointing out that the pattern is consistent with our hypothesis.

senses.label: THE MEASURE'S MAGNITUDE IS NOT ITS INFORMATION: temporal coding capability DOES NOT CORRESPOND TO THE MAGNITUDE OF THE MTF - LARGE ITC VALUES FOR THE ALPHA BAND DO NOT INDICATE HIGH TEMPORAL CODING CAPABILITY
senses.head: THE MEASURE'S MAGNITUDE IS NOT ITS INFORMATION: temporal coding capability DOES NOT CORRESPOND TO THE MAGNITUDE OF THE MTF
senses.gloss: LARGE ITC VALUES FOR THE ALPHA BAND DO NOT INDICATE HIGH TEMPORAL CODING CAPABILITY
senses.evidence: The classification results also reveal data patterns that have not been shown in previous findings on the MTF. As the MTF shows decreased neural responses with increasing modulation rate, it is plausible to conjecture that temporal coding for acoustic dynamics would also show such a pattern. However, as observed in the classification analysis, the temporal coding capability does not correspond to the magnitude of the MTF—large ITC values for the alpha band do not indicate high temporal coding capability.

senses.label: and phase carries what power does not - phase-based classification is significantly better than power-based, which was only slightly above chance
senses.head: and phase carries what power does not
senses.gloss: phase-based classification is significantly better than power-based, which was only slightly above chance
senses.evidence: A Stimulus-type × Classification source (phase classification or power classification) 2-way rmANOVA reveals the main effect of Classification source ( F (1,14) = 30.44, p < 0.001, η p 2 = 0.685), with the D′ of phase-based classification significantly larger than the D′ of power-based classification. To determine whether classification performance is better than chance (D′ = 0), a 1-sample t test with Bonferroni correction was applied on each stimulus type and each classification source. For phase classification, the performance of all stimulus types was better than chance (for θ sounds, t (14) = 6.19, p < 0.001, d = 1.60; for α sounds, t (14) = 6.40, p < 0.001, d = 1.65; for γ sounds, t (14) = 6.44, p < 0.001, d = 1.66). For power classification, classification performance of α sounds was significant ( t (14) = 4.73, p = 0.002, d = 1.22) as well as θ sounds ( t (14) = 3.10, p = 0.046, d = 0.80), but performance of power classification was only slightly above chance. These results demonstrate that phase patterns of cortical oscillations reliably encode the temporal dynamics of stimuli.

senses.label: A CONCEPT MOVED FROM SPACE TO TIME: whereas we typically address segregation of function IN THE SPATIAL DOMAIN, different regions specialised for different operations, HERE WE PROVIDE A COMPELLING EXAMPLE OF CORTICAL SEGREGATION OF FUNCTION IN THE TIME DOMAIN
senses.evidence: This design, however, builds in a hole in processing, a segregation of function between low and high processing rates—perhaps optimized for sensory sampling—by an intermediate rate, perhaps optimized for allocating attentional and memory resources and functionally inhibiting task- or stimulus-irrelevant actions. Whereas we typically address segregation of function in the spatial domain, i.e., different regions are specialized for different operations, here, we provide a compelling example of cortical segregation of function in the time domain.

senses.label: with the negative space named as design rather than as absence - this design BUILDS IN A HOLE IN PROCESSING, a segregation between low and high rates BY AN INTERMEDIATE RATE
senses.head: with the negative space named as design rather than as absence

senses.evidence: This design, however, builds in a hole in processing, a segregation of function between low and high processing rates—perhaps optimized for sensory sampling—by an intermediate rate, perhaps optimized for allocating attentional and memory resources and functionally inhibiting task- or stimulus-irrelevant actions. Whereas we typically address segregation of function in the spatial domain, i.e., different regions are specialized for different operations, here, we provide a compelling example of cortical segregation of function in the time domain.

senses.label: and the result is claimed as general because the stimuli were not speech: based on NONSPEECH stimuli, such dual-scale entrainment IS NOT SPEECH SPECIFIC but may rather reflect AN INTRINSIC AUDITORY PROCESSING PROPERTY
senses.evidence: Importantly, our results, based on nonspeech stimuli, suggest that such dual-scale entrainment is not speech specific but may rather reflect an intrinsic auditory processing property. The auditory cortex tunes to both theta frequency and gamma frequency acoustic dynamics [ 65 ]. The alpha band reflects different operations.

senses.label: a strictly hierarchical model ruled out in the introduction - short windows concatenated into longer ones CANNOT BY ITSELF MEET THE PERCEPTUAL DEMANDS
senses.head: a strictly hierarchical model ruled out in the introduction
senses.gloss: short windows concatenated into longer ones CANNOT BY ITSELF MEET THE PERCEPTUAL DEMANDS
senses.evidence: A strictly hierarchical model, starting, say, with short/small integration windows at more peripheral processing regions, which are then concatenated to build longer windows, cannot by itself meet the perceptual demands

senses.label: and the behavioral asymmetry that motivates everything: all clean stimuli identified well, with REDUCED PERFORMANCE IN CORRECTLY IDENTIFYING THE ALPHA SOUNDS ACROSS ALL LEVELS compared to both gamma and theta
senses.evidence: The results ( Fig 1b ) demonstrate that participants identified all clean stimuli well (all d′ > 2) and that performance deteriorated in all conditions as the SNR level decreased. Particularly noteworthy is the reduced performance in correctly identifying the α sounds across all levels compared to both γ and θ sounds.

senses.label: a time scale - THREE DIFFERENT SPANS UNDER ONE EXPRESSION: working memory milliseconds to minutes, short-term memory minutes to days, long-term memory up to what the authors put in scare quotes as 'infinity'; the phrase that organises the whole review denotes a different quantity in each of its three sections
senses.head: a time scale
senses.gloss: THREE DIFFERENT SPANS UNDER ONE EXPRESSION: working memory milliseconds to minutes, short-term memory minutes to days, long-term memory up to what the authors put in scare quotes as 'infinity'; the phrase that organises the whole review denotes a different quantity in each of its three sections
senses.evidence: Whereas the time scale of working memory is from milliseconds to minutes, short-term memory stores items on a time scale of minutes to days

senses.label: long-term memory's upper bound - IN THE AUTHORS' OWN SCARE QUOTES: given as up to 'infinity', with the immediate qualification that it is still under debate how items can be stored for such a long time, so the widest value in the review is the one marked as least settled

senses.evidence: Although the time scale of long-term memory could be up to “infinity,” it is still under debate how items can be stored for such a long time

senses.label: an eligibility trace - A MODELLING DEVICE WITHOUT ITS PHYSIOLOGY: named in 1943 and used in many learning-algorithm approaches to bridge time gaps, while the physiological basis of the longer traces is stated to be unclear, so the algorithms assume a mechanism the review declines to underwrite

senses.evidence: These so-called eligibility traces (Hull 1943; Rall 1967) are used in many approaches [e.g., Sutton (1988); Sutton and Barto (1998); Suri and Schultz (1999); Porr and Wörgötter (2003)] to bridge time gaps in learning algorithms, but the physiological basis of longer traces is unclear

senses.label: Low and High probability are stipulated as exactly one versus exactly four preceding standards, on the ground that prior work found no further change beyond four
senses.evidence: We used the terms of Low and High because prior studies have shown no difference between the RTs to targets if the number of the preceding standard stimuli were more than four 41 . Thus Low (Prob1) and High (Prob4) can be considered as most representative categories to describe the possible involvement of different target expectancy levels in task performance.

senses.label: pharmacologically validated means the study contains an agent known to produce an effect, so a null on the other agent is a null in a demonstrably sensitive assay
senses.evidence: Caffeine exposure also served as pharmacological (positive) control as it has been previously reported that intraoral administration of 3 mg/kg b.w. caffeine reliably improved cognitive functions and mood

senses.label: synergy is operationalised as a violation of additivity - the sum of single-agent effects against the combined condition, not as a simple interaction term
senses.head: synergy is operationalised as a violation of additivity
senses.gloss: the sum of single-agent effects against the combined condition, not as a simple interaction term
senses.evidence: To reveal potential interactions of caffeine and UMTS MP exposure in RT and oscillatory measures we focused on the exposure block and we used the additive analysis model with the following formula, as applied elsewhere 42 , 43 , 44 : Hereafter, “[Caffeine − Control] + [UMTS − Control]” and “Combined − Control” are referred to as ‘sum’ and ‘simultaneous’ data, respectively. We hypothesized that violation of the additivity of the analyzed RT or spectral amplitude measures would indicate synergistic interactions.

senses.label: THE CONFOUND, stated in one sentence and inherited by every subliminal-versus-supraliminal comparison in this corpus: in traditional masking paradigms the unconscious primes are also the WEAKER primes, so a smaller unconscious effect `might just be the result of a difference in signal strength, rather than a difference in awareness`. Two variables move together and the design cannot say which one did the work
senses.evidence: In traditional masking paradigms, unconscious primes typically have a lower signal strength than conscious primes, confounding the comparison between conscious and unconscious processing. As an alternative approach, we categorized trials with identical stimulus strength as either conscious, uncertain, or unconscious based on the trial-by-trial prime awareness assessment

senses.label: awareness as a PROPERTY OF A TRIAL rather than of a condition - the paradigm's whole move. Every prime has identical perceptual strength; the trials are sorted AFTERWARDS by what the participant reports seeing on that trial, into conscious, uncertain and unconscious. The experimenter no longer decides which trials were unconscious, and awareness stops being something the design asserts and becomes something it measures
senses.head: awareness as a PROPERTY OF A TRIAL rather than of a condition
senses.gloss: the paradigm's whole move. Every prime has identical perceptual strength; the trials are sorted AFTERWARDS by what the participant reports seeing on that trial, into conscious, uncertain and unconscious. The experimenter no longer decides which trials were unconscious, and awareness stops being something the design asserts and becomes something it measures
senses.evidence: Crucially, in all these conditions, the primes have identical perceptual strength. Significant priming was observed for all conditions, but the effects for conscious trials were significantly stronger, and no difference was observed between uncertain and unconscious trials

senses.label: the result in two halves, and the second is a NULL that shapes the first: significant priming in ALL THREE trial types, with conscious trials significantly stronger - and NO difference between uncertain and unconscious. So awareness matters with signal strength held constant, but the boundary behaves like a step between `saw it` and `did not clearly see it` rather than a gradient across the middle
senses.head: the result in two halves, and the second is a NULL that shapes the first: significant priming in ALL THREE trial types, with conscious trials significantly stronger
senses.gloss: and NO difference between uncertain and unconscious. So awareness matters with signal strength held constant, but the boundary behaves like a step between `saw it` and `did not clearly see it` rather than a gradient across the middle
senses.evidence: Significant priming was observed for all conditions, but the effects for conscious trials were significantly stronger, and no difference was observed between uncertain and unconscious trials. Thus, awareness of the prime has a large impact on congruency effects, even when signal strength is controlled for

senses.label: A METHODS PAPER REFUSING TO CROWN ITS OWN METHOD: `The aim of the current paper is not to suggest abolishing objective prime awareness measures OR TO PROVIDE A PERFECT MEASURE of prime awareness, but rather to explore alternative measures where consciousness is inferred from INTROSPECTION and where visual strength ... is perfectly matched.` It states what it trades - objective performance for self-report - instead of claiming to have escaped the trade-off
