senses.evidence: The aim of the current paper is not to suggest abolishing objective prime awareness measures or to provide a perfect measure of prime awareness, but rather to explore alternative measures where consciousness is inferred from introspection and where visual strength in conscious and unconscious conditions is perfectly matched

senses.label: two distinct senses of hippocampal sound response are proposed: a short-latency onset response, present even in sleep and not sound-specific, versus a longer sound-specific response that needs task engagement
senses.evidence: Based on the current findings and the results of previous experiments we described the existence of two types of hippocampal neuronal responses to sounds: sound-onset responses with very short latency and longer-lasting sound-specific responses that are likely to be present when the animal is actively engaged in the task.

senses.label: sound-responsive is defined by ANY of four a-priori bin sizes surviving FDR correction - a disjunctive criterion, so the label mixes fast transient and slow sustained responses
senses.head: sound-responsive is defined by ANY of four a-priori bin sizes surviving FDR correction
senses.gloss: a disjunctive criterion, so the label mixes fast transient and slow sustained responses
senses.evidence: A neuron was considered a “sound or reward-encoding” neuron if any of the time bins showed a corrected p -value smaller than 0.05.

senses.label: passive here means a different room, different floor, different light and different smell - the novelty of the context is part of the manipulation, not a nuisance
senses.head: passive here means a different room, different floor, different light and different smell
senses.gloss: the novelty of the context is part of the manipulation, not a nuisance
senses.evidence: Outside the context of the behavioral task, passive exposures to the awake rat were done in an unfamiliar dark plastic bin (33 × 22 × 35 cm) which differed from the training environment by geometry, texture of the floor and the walls, the lighting, and the smell.

senses.label: the earlier null from this group's own work is reinterpreted as an artefact of overtraining rather than as an absence of the phenomenon
senses.evidence: However, in those experiments hippocampal neurons did not respond to sounds when played to the animal not engaged in a discrimination task. These recordings were performed in highly over trained animals and it is possible that some of the features of neuronal responses were absent due to repetition of the same stimuli over many thousands of trials.

senses.label: echo response here means a response at the anticipated time AFTER the sound stops - it has nothing to do with acoustic echoes; the corpus also contains echo suppression in Muniak2014, where the echo is a real reflected sound
senses.head: echo response here means a response at the anticipated time AFTER the sound stops
senses.gloss: it has nothing to do with acoustic echoes; the corpus also contains echo suppression in Muniak2014, where the echo is a real reflected sound
senses.evidence: These studies have shown that repetitive stimulation at a regular inter-stimulus interval (ISI) can result in neuronal activity at the anticipated time interval after stimulation, a phenomenon known as “omitted stimulus-evoked responses” or “echo responses

senses.label: tonotopic organization is scale-dependent in this paper: present at about 1 mm, absent below 200 microns, so the same claim is true or false depending on the scale at which it is asserted
senses.evidence: The precise tonotopic organization in auditory cortex is a long debated issue 20 , 21 , 26 and remains unresolved. On the macroscopic scale level (~1 mm), the tonotopic map in the A1 arises from MGBv. However, the frequency selectivity of neighboring neurons can be very different, and no reliable tonotopic organization could be observed over spatial scales of <200 µm

senses.label: A1 is identified by thalamic connectivity from MGBv, not by the frequency responses being studied - an external criterion, as in Humphries2010's core/belt boundary
senses.head: A1 is identified by thalamic connectivity from MGBv, not by the frequency responses being studied
senses.gloss: an external criterion, as in Humphries2010's core/belt boundary
senses.evidence: To verify that the imaged cortical regions were located in the A1, we used the criterion 44 , 45 that the ventral part of the lateral medial geniculate body (MGBv) is connecting with A1.

senses.label: best frequency here is read off a Gaussian fit to 11 log-spaced frequencies between 2 and 40 kHz, each repeated 20 times
senses.evidence: To test the frequency tuning properties of single neurons, 11 frequencies logarithmically spaced in the range of 2–40 kHz were used in our experiment. Every frequency of stimulation was repeated 20 times, with the inter-stimulus interval (ISI) of 2 s.

senses.label: local heterogeneity - neighbouring neurons with very different tuning - is presented as embedded within the global tonotopic order rather than as its refutation
senses.head: local heterogeneity
senses.gloss: neighbouring neurons with very different tuning - is presented as embedded within the global tonotopic order rather than as its refutation
senses.evidence: Therefore, these studies demonstrate that a rough tonotopic organization emerges at large scales, but local heterogeneity emerges at fine scales (<250 μm) and is embedded in the global tonotopic order

senses.label: THE BORDER DEPENDS ON WHICH CLASSIFIER YOU PICK, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO BEFORE MOVING IT: THERE IS LITTLE AGREEMENT ON THE PRECISE BORDERS OF THE DIFFERENT NUCLEI OF THE IC, AND ITS PARCELLATION HAS BEEN DIFFERENT BASED ON WHETHER CELL MORPHOLOGY, INPUTS, OR PHYSIOLOGICAL PROPERTIES WERE CHOSEN AS THE MAIN CLASSIFIER - HERE WE USED PHYSIOLOGICAL PROPERTIES AS THE MAIN CRITERION
senses.head: THE BORDER DEPENDS ON WHICH CLASSIFIER YOU PICK, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO BEFORE MOVING IT: THERE IS LITTLE AGREEMENT ON THE PRECISE BORDERS OF THE DIFFERENT NUCLEI OF THE IC, AND ITS PARCELLATION HAS BEEN DIFFERENT BASED ON WHETHER CELL MORPHOLOGY, INPUTS, OR PHYSIOLOGICAL PROPERTIES WERE CHOSEN AS THE MAIN CLASSIFIER
senses.gloss: HERE WE USED PHYSIOLOGICAL PROPERTIES AS THE MAIN CRITERION
senses.evidence: There is little agreement on the precise borders of the different nuclei of the IC, and its parcellation has been different based on whether cell morphology, inputs, or physiological properties were chosen as the main classifier ( Oliver, 2005 ). Here we used physiological properties as the main criterion to look at the borders between the DCIC, LCIC and CNIC in the dorsal IC.

senses.label: AND TWO PUBLISHED ATLASES DRAW THE SAME DEMARCATION AT NINETY DEGREES TO EACH OTHER: THE MINIMUM FREQUENCY LINE ALIGNS WITH THE DEMARCATION FROM THE ALLEN REFERENCE ATLAS, WHILE THAT BY PAXINOS AND FRANKLIN LAYS IN THE ORTHOGONAL DIRECTION. Both are in current use; a coordinate tagged to one of them is not tagged to the other
senses.evidence: We overlaid the line representing the neurons with the lowest CF and compared its location with the border of LCIC and DCIC traced from the latest Allen Reference Atlas (CCFv3) and from the classical reference atlas by Paxinos and Franklin (2001) . The minimum frequency line aligns with the demarcation from the Allen Reference Atlas, while that by Paxinos and Franklin lays in the orthogonal direction.

senses.label: THE FEATURE THAT DEFINES ONE SIDE IS FOUND ON BOTH SIDES: SURPRISINGLY, WE OBSERVED GAD67-DENSE MODULES IN BOTH THE MEDIAL AND THE LATERAL ASPECT OF THE IC, THAT IS WITHIN BOTH LCIC AND DCIC IN EITHER ATLAS - and the modules are A DEFINING FEATURE OF THE LCIC
senses.head: THE FEATURE THAT DEFINES ONE SIDE IS FOUND ON BOTH SIDES: SURPRISINGLY, WE OBSERVED GAD67-DENSE MODULES IN BOTH THE MEDIAL AND THE LATERAL ASPECT OF THE IC, THAT IS WITHIN BOTH LCIC AND DCIC IN EITHER ATLAS
senses.gloss: and the modules are A DEFINING FEATURE OF THE LCIC
senses.evidence: Surprisingly, we observed GAD67-dense modules in both the medial and the lateral aspect of the IC (arrowheads Figure 9A,G ), that is within both LCIC and DCIC in either atlas.

senses.label: the claim the title rests on is a direction, not a location: THE SOLID LINE SHOWS THE BEST POLYNOMIAL FIT, WHICH EXPLAINED AROUND 13% OF THE VARIANCE IN CFs. The organisation is real and it predicts almost nothing about any individual cell
senses.evidence: The solid line in Figure 6B shows the best polynomial fit, which explained around 13% of the variance in CFs.

senses.label: and the paper says the variability is not measurement error: WE FOUND CONSIDERABLE VARIABILITY IN CFs WITHIN A BAND, and SUBSTANTIAL VARIABILITY WAS ALSO OBSERVED WITHIN A SINGLE ANIMAL
senses.evidence: We found considerable variability in CFs within a band. Imprecisions in the alignment of imaging areas and variability between animals may have contributed to the variability, but substantial variability was also observed within a single animal, in line with previous results

senses.label: A SAMPLING BIAS NAMED WITH ITS PHYSICAL CAUSE: THERE WAS AN OVER-REPRESENTATION OF LOW CF NEURONS IN THE DEEPEST REGIONS, attributed to THE LOW FREQUENCY REGION COINCIDING WITH THE CENTER OF THE CRANIAL WINDOW, WHERE IT WAS POSSIBLE TO IMAGE SOMEWHAT DEEPER THAN TOWARDS THE EDGES - the optics of the window, not the tissue
senses.head: A SAMPLING BIAS NAMED WITH ITS PHYSICAL CAUSE: THERE WAS AN OVER-REPRESENTATION OF LOW CF NEURONS IN THE DEEPEST REGIONS, attributed to THE LOW FREQUENCY REGION COINCIDING WITH THE CENTER OF THE CRANIAL WINDOW, WHERE IT WAS POSSIBLE TO IMAGE SOMEWHAT DEEPER THAN TOWARDS THE EDGES
senses.gloss: the optics of the window, not the tissue
senses.evidence: There was an over-representation of low CF neurons in the deepest regions (121–160 μm deep, Figure 6E,F ). We attribute this to a sampling bias in which the low frequency region coincided with the center of the cranial window, where it was possible to image somewhat deeper than towards the edges

senses.label: THE IDENTITY OF WHAT WAS MEASURED IS LEFT OPEN: WHILE WE DO NOT EXCLUDE THE POSSIBILITY OF IMAGING INTO THE CENTRAL NUCLEUS OF THE IC, WE BELIEVE THE OBSERVED TONOTOPY TO BE A GOOD REPRESENTATION OF THE IC SHELL REGION
senses.evidence: While we do not exclude the possibility of imaging into the central nucleus of the IC, we believe the observed tonotopy to be a good representation of the IC shell region because all CFs were represented among the most superficial neurons

senses.label: TWO CLASSES OF RESPONSE EXIST BECAUSE THE ANIMAL WAS AWAKE AND THE TONE WAS LONG: INHIBITORY AND OFFSET RESPONSES WERE NOT REPORTED IN EARLIER IMAGING EXPERIMENTS PERFORMED IN ANESTHETIZED MICE, and THEIR USE OF SHORTER STIMULI DID NOT ALLOW A DISTINCTION BETWEEN ONSET AND SUSTAINED RESPONSES. Two conditions, two whole response categories
senses.evidence: Inhibitory and offset responses were not reported in earlier imaging experiments performed in anesthetized mice ( Ito et al., 2014 ; Barnstedt et al., 2015 ); their use of shorter stimuli did not allow a distinction between onset and sustained responses.

senses.label: and the size of that difference is stated against a named earlier number: THE PROPORTION OF CELLS SHOWING SOUND-EVOKED INHIBITION WAS CLEARLY HIGHER THAN THE 2-23% REPORTED FOR ANESTHETIZED C57BL/6 MICE
senses.evidence: The proportion of cells showing sound-evoked inhibition was clearly higher than the 2–23% reported for anesthetized C57BL/6 mice in Willott et al. (1988a)

senses.label: OFFSET RESPONSES ARE GENERALLY RESTRICTED TO CELLS SHOWING BAND-PASS DURATION TUNING, WHICH ONLY RESPONDED TO MUCH SHORTER TONES THAN THE 1 S EMPLOYED HERE - so finding them at all is the finding
senses.head: OFFSET RESPONSES ARE GENERALLY RESTRICTED TO CELLS SHOWING BAND-PASS DURATION TUNING, WHICH ONLY RESPONDED TO MUCH SHORTER TONES THAN THE 1 S EMPLOYED HERE
senses.gloss: so finding them at all is the finding
senses.evidence: However, studies in the IC of anesthetized mice, rats and chinchillas showed that offset responses are generally restricted to cells showing band-pass duration tuning, which only responded to much shorter tones than the 1 s employed here ( Chen, 1998 ; Brand et al., 2000 ; Pérez-González et al., 2006 ). Another striking finding was therefore that we saw clear evidence for offset responses in 3–11% of sound-responsive cells.

senses.label: TWO EARLIER PAPERS REPORTED GRADIENTS IN DIFFERENT DIRECTIONS AND THIS ONE IS COMPATIBLE WITH BOTH: ITO ET AL. REPORTED GRADIENTS RUNNING FROM LATERAL (LOW-FREQUENCY) TO MEDIAL (HIGH-FREQUENCY), WHEREAS BARNSTEDT ET AL. REPORTED GRADIENTS IN A MEDIOROSTRAL TO LATEROCAUDAL DIRECTION - a reversal makes two opposite gradients the same finding, seen from two sides of the minimum
senses.head: TWO EARLIER PAPERS REPORTED GRADIENTS IN DIFFERENT DIRECTIONS AND THIS ONE IS COMPATIBLE WITH BOTH: ITO ET AL. REPORTED GRADIENTS RUNNING FROM LATERAL (LOW-FREQUENCY) TO MEDIAL (HIGH-FREQUENCY), WHEREAS BARNSTEDT ET AL. REPORTED GRADIENTS IN A MEDIOROSTRAL TO LATEROCAUDAL DIRECTION
senses.gloss: a reversal makes two opposite gradients the same finding, seen from two sides of the minimum
senses.evidence: Interestingly, our data are also compatible with two earlier two-photon calcium imaging studies ( Ito et al., 2014 ; Barnstedt et al., 2015 ). Ito et al. (2014) reported gradients in the medial regions of the dorsal IC, which ran from lateral (low-frequency) to medial (high-frequency), whereas Barnstedt et al. (2015) reported gradients in a mediorostral to laterocaudal direction.

senses.label: THE SAME MEASUREMENT MADE IN A neighborING STRUCTURE GIVES THE OPPOSITE ANSWER: OUR RESULTS THUS DIFFER FROM AUDITORY CORTEX, WHERE LOCAL MICROHETEROGENEITY IS MUCH SMALLER FOR (PARVALBUMIN-POSITIVE) GABAERGIC NEURONS THAN FOR GLUTAMATERGIC NEURONS, and here THE MICROHETEROGENEITY WAS SIMILAR FOR GABAERGIC AND GLUTAMATERGIC NEURONS
senses.evidence: Our results thus differ from auditory cortex, where response patterns are different and local microheterogeneity is much smaller for (parvalbumin-positive) GABAergic neurons than for glutamatergic neurons ( Maor et al., 2016 ; Liang et al., 2018 ; Liu et al., 2019 ). We conclude that despite the shared input and firing behavior during development ( Babola et al., 2018 ), functional heterogeneity dominates within bands in the dorsal IC of adult mice.

senses.label: and one candidate cause of a disagreement is the indicator, not the tissue: THIS MICROHETEROGENEITY WAS LARGER THAN IN AN EARLIER STUDY IN WHICH BULK LOADING OF AN ORGANIC Ca INDICATOR WAS USED, WHICH MAY HAVE MADE IT MORE DIFFICULT TO ISOLATE RESPONSES FROM INDIVIDUAL CELLS
senses.evidence: This microheterogeneity was larger than in an earlier study in which bulk loading of an organic Ca indicator was used ( Ito et al., 2014 ), which may have made it more difficult to isolate responses from individual cells.

senses.label: THE COUNT THAT SURVIVES TWO EXCLUSIONS IS THE ONE REPORTED: 165 (OUT OF 1359) CELLS SHOWED A POSITIVE CORRELATION WITH FACIAL MOVEMENTS, and IN THE END, 41 CELLS SHOWED SPONTANEOUS CALCIUM TRANSIENTS THAT CORRELATED WITH ANIMAL MOVEMENT AND THAT COULD NOT BE EXPLAINED BY THEIR FRA
senses.evidence: By correlating movement and fluorescence, we detected 165 (out of 1359) cells that showed a positive correlation ( r > 0.25) with facial movements during the spontaneous recording period. To exclude potential false-positive detection due to motion artefacts (i.e. cells moving into and out of focus), we excluded cells with fluorescence transients that did not show the typical ~1 s exponential decay kinetics, which last much longer than the brief image shifts that could accompany movement events (image shifts in Figure 8A , Figure 8—figure supplement 1 ). Since animal movement inevitably produces sound that may activate the IC neurons, leading to an apparent movement sensitivity, we also excluded the cells that showed excitatory or offset responses in their FRA. In the end, 41 cells showed spontaneous calcium transients that correlated with animal movement and that could not be explained by their FRA, which was either inhibited-type or showed no clear pure tone evoked responses

senses.label: A NEGATIVE THAT DOES THE ARGUMENTATIVE WORK: MOVEMENT-SENSITIVE NEURONS WERE NOT FOUND IN THE HIGH-FREQUENCY DCIC REGIONS, BUT ONLY IN THE PUTATIVE CNIC REGION AND THE LCIC. The border is drawn by where the cells are ABSENT
senses.evidence: Movement-sensitive neurons were not found in the high-frequency DCIC regions, but only in the putative CNIC region and the LCIC.

senses.label: and the detection method could not have found the effect the literature predicts: FOR SOMATOSENSORY INPUTS, THE DOMINANT EFFECT APPEARS TO BE INHIBITORY, WHICH WOULD NOT HELP DETECTION BASED ON OUR SELECTION CRITERIA
senses.evidence: For somatosensory inputs, the dominant effect appears to be inhibitory and only a minority of cells have been shown to respond to unimodal tactile stimuli ( Aitkin et al., 1978 ; Aitkin et al., 1981 ; Zhou and Shore, 2006 ), which would not help detection based on our selection criteria.

senses.label: AN EVIDENTIAL STATUS STATED IN THE TEXT: WE OBTAINED ANECDOTAL EVIDENCE THAT NEURONS AT THE BORDER OF THE MODULES CAN EXTEND DENDRITES INTO THE MODULES. The mechanism that answers the paper's own open question is offered as anecdote, in the authors' own word
senses.evidence: We obtained anecdotal evidence that neurons at the border of the modules can extend dendrites into the modules ( Figure 10A,F ), which would allow them to sample non-auditory inputs.

senses.label: and the question it answers is stated as a problem for the field, not for this paper: THESE INPUTS TARGET THE LAYER TWO MODULES, WHICH CONSTITUTE ONLY A SMALL FRACTION OF THE LCIC VOLUME - THIS RAISES THE QUESTION HOW SO MANY CELLS IN THE LCIC CAN BE SENSITIVE TO NON-AUDITORY INPUTS
senses.head: and the question it answers is stated as a problem for the field, not for this paper: THESE INPUTS TARGET THE LAYER TWO MODULES, WHICH CONSTITUTE ONLY A SMALL FRACTION OF THE LCIC VOLUME
senses.gloss: THIS RAISES THE QUESTION HOW SO MANY CELLS IN THE LCIC CAN BE SENSITIVE TO NON-AUDITORY INPUTS
senses.evidence: These inputs target the layer two modules, which constitute only a small fraction of the LCIC volume. Moreover, neurons in the modules do not seem to target extramodular IC neurons ( Lesicko and Llano, 2019 ). This raises the question how so many cells in the LCIC can be sensitive to non-auditory inputs.

senses.label: THE LABEL IS PURE IN ONE DIRECTION ONLY: 95% OF GCaMP-POSITIVE NEURONS IN THE GP4.3 LINE WERE NOT POSITIVE FOR GAD67, and NOT ALL NON-GABAERGIC CELLS WERE GCaMP-POSITIVE - what the label includes is known, what it misses is not
senses.head: THE LABEL IS PURE IN ONE DIRECTION ONLY: 95% OF GCaMP-POSITIVE NEURONS IN THE GP4.3 LINE WERE NOT POSITIVE FOR GAD67, and NOT ALL NON-GABAERGIC CELLS WERE GCaMP-POSITIVE
senses.gloss: what the label includes is known, what it misses is not
senses.evidence: The large majority (4651/4898; 95%) of GCaMP-positive neurons in the GP4.3 line were not positive for GAD67 ( Figure 1A–D ), showing that the Thy1-promoter preferentially expressed GCaMP6s in non-GABAergic cells in the IC

senses.label: the same asymmetry in the other line: GAD67 IMMUNOREACTIVITY was detected IN >93% OF GCaMP-POSITIVE NEURONS IN THE Gad2;Ai96 MICE, and NOT ALL GAD67-POSITIVE CELLS IN THIS MOUSE LINE WERE LABELED BY GCaMP6s
senses.evidence: In contrast, we detected GAD67 immunoreactivity in >93% (1702/1828) of GCaMP-positive neurons in the Gad2;Ai96 mice ( Figure 1D,H–O ). Not all GAD67-positive cells in this mouse line were labeled by GCaMP6s

senses.label: A MARKER THAT DOES NOT PLACE A CELL: AT THE SINGLE NEURON LEVEL, THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF THE TWO BUFFERS WAS INSUFFICIENT TO INDICATE WHETHER THE NEURONS LAY WITHIN A MODULE
senses.evidence: At the single neuron level, the presence or absence of the two buffers was insufficient to indicate whether the neurons lay within a module. These results suggest that for both lines there is not a clear enrichment of GCaMP6+ neurons within the neurochemical modules.

senses.label: THE CLASS WITHOUT GROUND TRUTH IS NAMED: DUE TO THEIR RARITY, WE HAVE NOT OBTAINED A SIMULTANEOUS RECORDING FOR OFFSET CELLS - every other response class was verified against spikes in the same cell and this one was not
senses.head: THE CLASS WITHOUT GROUND TRUTH IS NAMED: DUE TO THEIR RARITY, WE HAVE NOT OBTAINED A SIMULTANEOUS RECORDING FOR OFFSET CELLS
senses.gloss: every other response class was verified against spikes in the same cell and this one was not
senses.evidence: Due to their rarity, we have not obtained a simultaneous recording for offset cells.

senses.label: the difference between the two cell classes is one measurement and it is a size: GABAERGIC CELLS HAD A LARGER SOMA SIZE, AS REPORTED PREVIOUSLY, and WITHIN EACH GENOTYPE, SOMA SIZE DID NOT DIFFER SIGNIFICANTLY AMONG CELLS WITH DIFFERENT FRA CLASSES
senses.evidence: GABAergic cells had a larger soma size, as reported previously (cat: Oliver et al., 1994 ; rat: Merchán et al., 2005 ). The estimated diameters for Gad2;Ai96 and GP4.3 cells, defined as 4/π times the square root of the ROI area in imaging experiments, were 21.9 ± 4.9 µm (mean ±s.d.) and 15.9 ± 2.6 µm, respectively ( Figure 4C , p<0.001 Wilcoxon Rank Test). Within each genotype, soma size did not differ significantly among cells with different FRA classes.

senses.label: and the conclusion is stated as a definition rather than a discovery: OUR EXPERIMENTS THUS PROVIDE A FUNCTIONAL DEFINITION OF THE MAJOR ORGANIZATION PRINCIPLES OF THE DORSAL IC IN ADULT MICE
senses.evidence: We investigated the functional organization of the dorsal IC in awake mice at the single neuron level. We found that the dorsal IC is tonotopically organized, with isofrequency bands running in a rostrolateral-caudomedial orientation with frequency tuning varying along the caudolateral-rostromedial direction. The lowest CF band was found in the middle, dividing the dorsal IC into two reversed tonotopic gradients. In the caudolateral part, but not in the rostromedial part, neurons that were sensitive to whisker or other movements were found, which was in agreement with the view that the caudolateral and rostromedial part corresponded to the LCIC and DCIC, respectively. We observed four different types of firing patterns in response to tones, but other than the tonotopical organization, no obvious topographical organization was observed for the firing patterns. GABAergic neurons were on average somewhat larger, but otherwise there were not clear differences with glutamatergic neurons in spatial organization or firing patterns. Our experiments thus provide a functional definition of the major organization principles of the dorsal IC in adult mice.

senses.label: cognitive load - operationalised here as TWO components, mental load and mental effort, inside a model that also carries technology-acceptance and motivation constructs
senses.head: cognitive load
senses.gloss: operationalised here as TWO components, mental load and mental effort, inside a model that also carries technology-acceptance and motivation constructs
senses.evidence: Technology usage in STEAM education also has the benefits of decreasing cognitive load (mental load and mental effort) and improving students’ learning intentions

senses.label: generalization - established by a NON-SIGNIFICANT group difference rather than by sampling both populations to a defined standard
senses.head: generalization
senses.gloss: established by a NON-SIGNIFICANT group difference rather than by sampling both populations to a defined standard
senses.evidence: Therefore, our research result can be interpreted as generalization for both elementary and university students.

senses.label: `cognitive load` - A TWO-PART PARTITION WHOSE HALVES ARE EASILY CONFLATED, AND THIS PAPER KEEPS THEM APART. `COGNITIVE LOAD CONSISTS OF TWO CONSTRUCTS: MENTAL LOAD AND MENTAL EFFORT.` The names differ by one word and both read as `how hard it feels`. **The distinction is between what the TASK imposes and what the LEARNER expends**, and a corpus that carries only one of the two - as this record did - silently makes `cognitive load` mean whichever half it kept.
senses.head: `cognitive load`
senses.gloss: A TWO-PART PARTITION WHOSE HALVES ARE EASILY CONFLATED, AND THIS PAPER KEEPS THEM APART. `COGNITIVE LOAD CONSISTS OF TWO CONSTRUCTS: MENTAL LOAD AND MENTAL EFFORT.` The names differ by one word and both read as `how hard it feels`. **The distinction is between what the TASK imposes and what the LEARNER expends**, and a corpus that carries only one of the two - as this record did - silently makes `cognitive load` mean whichever half it kept.
senses.evidence: Cognitive load consists of two constructs: mental load and mental effort.

senses.label: `ARCS` - AN ACRONYM WHOSE LETTERS ARE ITS PARTITION, LIKE `WEIRD` IN `henrich2010`. `The ARCS theory construct CONSISTS OF FOUR SUB-CONSTRUCTS: ATTENTION, RELEVANCE, CONFIDENCE, AND SATISFACTION (SAT).` The name cannot drift from its content because the content spells the name - **and the same sentence then gives `satisfaction` a SECOND abbreviation, `SAT`, so one construct carries two acronyms at different levels.**
senses.head: `ARCS`
senses.gloss: AN ACRONYM WHOSE LETTERS ARE ITS PARTITION, LIKE `WEIRD` IN `henrich2010`. `The ARCS theory construct CONSISTS OF FOUR SUB-CONSTRUCTS: ATTENTION, RELEVANCE, CONFIDENCE, AND SATISFACTION (SAT).` The name cannot drift from its content because the content spells the name - **and the same sentence then gives `satisfaction` a SECOND abbreviation, `SAT`, so one construct carries two acronyms at different levels.**
senses.evidence: The ARCS theory construct consists of four sub-constructs: attention, relevance, confidence, and satisfaction (SAT)

senses.label: A PREDICTION IS STATED AS A CONDITIONAL AND THEN FALSIFIED BY THE AUTHORS' OWN EXPERIMENT: if the pathway specifically carries noise, then inactivation would block the noise-trained response BUT NOT the tone-trained one
senses.evidence: If the septo-hippocampal pathway is a route that specifically carries the noise bursts information, then MS inactivation would block the behavioral response trained with noise bursts but not those trained with tone bursts. Therefore, we studied whether the behavioral responses to noise bursts (80 dB SPL) and tone bursts (80 dB SPL) were affected by MS inactivation.

senses.label: and the result is reported as such - UNEXPECTEDLY, inactivation blocked not only the noise-induced freezing but also the tone-induced responses
senses.head: and the result is reported as such
senses.gloss: UNEXPECTEDLY, inactivation blocked not only the noise-induced freezing but also the tone-induced responses
senses.evidence: These results indicated that MS inactivation induced mice amnesia, but A1 inactivation did not. Unexpectedly, MS inactivation blocked not only the noise-induced freezing responses but also the tone-induced responses.

senses.label: TWO DISAGREEMENTS WITH THE LITERATURE, EACH ATTRIBUTED TO A DIFFERENT METHODOLOGICAL PARAMETER: one to the drug, since lidocaine lasts 10-15 minutes and muscimol more than an hour
senses.evidence: Although a previous study assumed that the MS is not required for auditory-cue fear conditioning ( Calandreau et al., 2007 ), possible explanations for the discrepancy between this previous study and our findings are the several technical and methodological differences. The previous study used lidocaine to inactivate the MS, the effects of which last approximately 10–15 min; in this study, we used muscimol to inactivate the MS and thereby block the acquisition of auditory fear conditioning completely.

senses.label: and one to the conditioning paradigm - a contemporary study found the opposite using delay conditioning where this one used trace conditioning
senses.head: and one to the conditioning paradigm
senses.gloss: a contemporary study found the opposite using delay conditioning where this one used trace conditioning
senses.evidence: However, recently, a study indicated that silencing the MS during conditioning specifically reduced noise-conditioned ( Zhang et al., 2018 ). This was not consistent with our results. Our results showed that the inactivation of the MS during conditioning blocked both the noise- and tone-conditioned fear responses ( Figure 8C ). The explanation for the discrepancy may be due to the different behavioral training procedures; we used trace fear conditioning model in this study, whereas they adopted delay fear conditioning. Another reason is that the MS inactivation may have disrupted fear conditioning through other mechanisms.

senses.label: THE DRUG WAS CHOSEN FOR ITS HALF-LIFE, before the disagreement arose: muscimol lasts long enough for the long-lasting training, which is the same property later used to explain the other laboratory's null
senses.evidence: The MS was inactivated by an injection of muscimol (an agonist of GABA A receptors). Its effect lasts more than 1 h ( Martin and Ghez, 1999 ), and the half-life time of its effect is longer than that of lidocaine ( Martin and Ghez, 1999 ). Therefore, the inactivation of the MS with muscimol lasts long enough for the long-lasting auditory fear training.

senses.label: THE INSTRUMENT DECIDES THE SIGN OF THE FINDING: whole-cell recording shows hyperpolarization to a tone, extracellular recording shows spikes, and the data from the two APPEAR DIFFERENT
senses.evidence: A recent study using an in vivo whole-cell recording technique showed that the auditory responses of most hippocampal CA1 neurons involve hyperpolarization following the onset of a tonal stimulus, but only in awake animals ( Abe et al., 2014 ). Hyperpolarization itself does not evoke action potentials, but its rebound depolarization does. Thus, the data obtained by whole-cell recordings appear different from those that are extracellularly recorded.

senses.label: and the same is said of the anaesthetic - earlier studies did record auditory responses in anesthetized animals, which may be due to differences in extracellular recording and or anaesthetics
senses.head: and the same is said of the anaesthetic
senses.gloss: earlier studies did record auditory responses in anesthetized animals, which may be due to differences in extracellular recording and or anaesthetics
senses.evidence: The non-lemniscal pathway, or the limbic system, is sensitive to temperature and drugs, especially to anesthetics ( Vinogradova, 1975 ; Dickinson et al., 2003 ; Kaifosh et al., 2013 ). This is why the noise-evoked responses were blocked by sodium pentobarbital ( Figure 1 ). Therefore, auditory sub-threshold responses have been recorded only in awake subjects ( Abe et al., 2014 ). However, several studies have recorded auditory evoked potentials and single units in anesthetized animals ( Miller and Freedman, 1995 ; Krause et al., 2003 ; Dissanayake et al., 2008 ). This may have been due to the differences in extracellular recording and/or anesthetics.

senses.label: A DISSOCIATION BETWEEN LEARNING AND REMEMBERING: during acquisition every group froze alike with no differences among them, and a day later the inactivated groups had nothing
senses.evidence: During acquisition training, all groups of mice showed increased freezing ( Figure 8B ), but there were no differences among them [repeated-measures ANOVA, F (3,15) = 0.838, P = 0.494]. In the retention testing 24 h after the conditioning, however, the average freezing response of the Mus-N (6.17 ± 1.28) and Mus-T (7.41 ± 2.09) mice was significantly lower than that of the Sal-N (51.89 ± 8.65) and Sal-T mice [51.92 ± 11.91, one-way ANOVA, F (3,20) = 18.374, P < 0.001, Scheffe test: Sal-N vs. Mus-N, P < 0.001; and Sal-T vs. Mus-T, P < 0.001], whereas the freezing responses between the Mus-N and Mus-T and the Sal-N and Sal-T mice were not different

senses.label: A CONNECTIVITY CLAIM INFERRED FROM A RANK ORDER OF MEANS: 15.7 ms before 19-21 ms before 24.6 ms, which is read as the direction the information travels
senses.evidence: We calculated the grand average latencies for the MS, EC, CA3, CA1, and A1 (15.731 ± 5.296, 19.385 ± 6.151, 19.709 ± 5.567, 21.217 ± 5.716, and 24.556 ± 6.914, respectively) ( Figure 4C ). The one-way ANOVA statistic indicated that the average latency for MS neurons was significantly shorter than that of the EC, CA3, CA1, or A1 neurons [ F (4,329) = 14.979, P < 0.001; Scheffe test, MS vs. EC: P = 0.028, MS vs. CA3: P = 0.005, MS vs. CA1: P < 0.001, and MS vs. A1: P < 0.001]. The average latencies for the EC, CA3, and CA regions were significantly shorter than was that of A1 (EC vs. A1: P < 0.001; CA3 vs. A1: P < 0.001; and CA1 vs. A1: P = 0.049), and the average latencies of the EC, CA3, and CA1 were not significantly different from each other

senses.label: with the inference stated as such - since one latency was longer and the other shorter, it is MOST LIKELY that the information comes from the non-lemniscal pathway
senses.head: with the inference stated as such
senses.gloss: since one latency was longer and the other shorter, it is MOST LIKELY that the information comes from the non-lemniscal pathway
senses.evidence: Since the A1 latency was longer and the MS latency was shorter than the CA3 and CA1 latencies, it is most likely that auditory information sent to the hippocampus comes from the non-lemniscal pathway, not the lemniscal one.

senses.label: A PATHWAY IDENTIFIED BY A BUNDLE OF RESPONSE PROPERTIES rather than by tracing: not tonotopic, broadly tuned, rapidly adapting, multisensory - so detailed study of the properties can tell which pathway is operating
senses.head: A PATHWAY IDENTIFIED BY A BUNDLE OF RESPONSE PROPERTIES rather than by tracing: not tonotopic, broadly tuned, rapidly adapting, multisensory
senses.gloss: so detailed study of the properties can tell which pathway is operating
senses.evidence: Lemniscal neurons are tonotopically organized ( Aitkin and Webster, 1972 ; Webster et al., 1992 ; Winer and Schreiner, 2011 ), narrowly tuned to a specific single frequency, and respond to repetitive tonal stimuli with fidelity. However, non-lemniscal neurons are not tonotopically organized, but are broadly frequency tuned, are able to rapidly adapt to repetitive identical stimuli ( Aitkin and Webster, 1972 ; Phillips and Irvine, 1979 ), and are involved in multisensory integration, temporal pattern recognition, and certain forms of learning ( Webster et al., 1992 ). Therefore, detailed studies of the response properties of hippocampal neurons can tell us which pathway is predominantly operating.

senses.label: AND THE PAPER SEPARATES TWO THINGS THAT ARE USUALLY RUN TOGETHER: that responses to a conditioned sound are enhanced by training DOES NOT MEAN the neurons respond to that sound
senses.evidence: Auditory responses of some hippocampal neurons to a conditioned sound are enhanced by auditory fear conditioning training ( O’Keefe and Nadel, 1978 ; Moita et al., 2003 ). However, this finding does not mean that hippocampal neurons respond to a conditioned sound. In other words, if some hippocampal neurons respond to some characterized sound, whether this sound is a more efficient conditioned sound in auditory fear conditioning in evoking behavioral responses, such as freezing, remains to be determined. Thus, what is the role of the responses of hippocampal neurons?

senses.label: the phenomenon exists only in one state - responses and spontaneous discharges fade within a minute of anesthesia and recover over the next fifty
senses.head: the phenomenon exists only in one state
senses.gloss: responses and spontaneous discharges fade within a minute of anesthesia and recover over the next fifty
senses.evidence: The auditory response and spontaneous discharges both faded away within 1 min of the injection, and they gradually recovered over the 50 min thereafter

senses.label: and the conditioned response generalizes completely across frequency, so a mouse trained on one tone freezes to all of them
senses.evidence: These results indicated that the freezing response induced by auditory fear conditioning was independent of the frequency of the sound used as the CS.

senses.label: THE CATEGORY DOES NOT CARVE, AND THE REVIEW SAYS SO IN ITS OWN VOICE: THESE APPROACHES TYPICALLY PRODUCE PARTIALLY OVERLAPPING CATEGORIES, PRODUCING AN INEVITABLE TENSION BETWEEN THE TENDENCY TO BE A “LUMPER” OR A “SPLITTER.”
senses.evidence: These approaches typically produce partially overlapping categories, producing an inevitable tension between the tendency to be a “lumper” or a “splitter.”

senses.label: AND THE UNCERTAINTY IS QUANTIFIED RATHER THAN HEDGED: THE TRUE NUMBER OF DISTINCT SUBTYPES OF SOM CELLS IS UNKNOWN, and it MOST LIKELY LIES SOMEWHERE BETWEEN 4 AND 100 SUBTYPES. A twenty-five-fold range on how many kinds of thing the name refers to, printed as the review's own estimate
senses.evidence: Thus while the true number of distinct subtypes of SOM cells is unknown, we estimate that it most likely lies somewhere between 4 and 100 subtypes.

senses.label: the upper bound is a count of what has NOT BEEN RULED OUT, not of what has been seen: THESE ASSUMPTIONS ARE POORLY CONSTRAINED BY DATA BECAUSE MOST STUDIES HAVE MEASURED ONLY A SUBSET OF THESE CRITERIA, and ADDITIONAL DATA THAT FURTHER CONSTRAINS THE NUMBER OF POSSIBLE COMBINATIONS WOULD REDUCE THIS NUMBER
senses.evidence: Estimating such an upper bound requires several assumptions about whether classification criteria can vary independently (producing all possible combinations) or whether there are correlations that reduce the number of combinations. These assumptions are poorly constrained by data because most studies have measured only a subset of these criteria. In addition, we assume here that these criteria are static, although it's likely that some criteria could change over time.

senses.label: ONE CRITERION CANNOT IDENTIFY THE CLASS: SOM-POSITIVE CELLS CAN ALSO EXHIBIT TONIC FAST SPIKING FIRING PROPERTIES AND PV-POSITIVE NEURONS CAN BE STUTTERING FAST SPIKING, WHICH INDICATES THAT DIFFERENT CELLS TYPES CAN HAVE SIMILAR FIRING PROPERTIES AND THUS THIS CRITERION ALONE CAN NOT BE USED TO RELIABLY IDENTIFY A SPECIFIC CELL TYPE
senses.evidence: In piriform cortex, SOM-positive cells can also exhibit tonic fast spiking firing properties and PV-positive neurons can be stuttering fast spiking, which indicates that different cells types can have similar firing properties and thus this criterion alone can not be used to reliably identify a specific cell type

senses.label: AND THE SAME CRITERION CAN FAIL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE: CLASSIFICATION OF SOM CELLS BASED ON FIRING PROPERTIES ALONE COULD LUMP TOGETHER DISTINCT CLASSES OR ERRONEOUSLY SPLIT A SINGLE CLASS, DEPENDING ON THE SAMPLE BEING STUDIED. Not a bias with a direction - a bias whose direction is set by whoever's cells you happen to have
senses.head: AND THE SAME CRITERION CAN FAIL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE: CLASSIFICATION OF SOM CELLS BASED ON FIRING PROPERTIES ALONE COULD LUMP TOGETHER DISTINCT CLASSES OR ERRONEOUSLY SPLIT A SINGLE CLASS, DEPENDING ON THE SAMPLE BEING STUDIED. Not a bias with a direction
senses.gloss: a bias whose direction is set by whoever's cells you happen to have
senses.evidence: It seems likely that classification of SOM cells based on firing properties alone (such as the tendency to burst) could lump together distinct classes or erroneously split a single class, depending on the sample being studied.

senses.label: A DISTINCTION THAT EXISTS IN THE TOOL AND NOT IN THE TISSUE: L4 SOM CELLS MAY BE A SINGLE POPULATION, WITH NO APPARENT FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF THEIR SEGREGATION INTO X94 AND NON-X94 CATEGORIES. The line drew the boundary; nothing measured since has found anything on either side of it
senses.evidence: Thus it appears that L4 SOM cells may be a single population, with no apparent functional correlates of their segregation into X94 and non-X94 categories

senses.label: IT IS STILL NOT CLEAR WHETHER LTS AND BURSTING SOM CELLS FORM TWO DISTINCT CATEGORIES OR INSTEAD ARE A SINGLE CLASS THAT LIE ALONG A CONTINUUM - the question of whether two names name two things, left open in the review's own words
senses.head: IT IS STILL NOT CLEAR WHETHER LTS AND BURSTING SOM CELLS FORM TWO DISTINCT CATEGORIES OR INSTEAD ARE A SINGLE CLASS THAT LIE ALONG A CONTINUUM
senses.gloss: the question of whether two names name two things, left open in the review's own words
senses.evidence: It is still not clear whether LTS and bursting SOM cells form two distinct categories or instead are a single class that lie along a continuum.

senses.label: and the disagreement may be nothing but vocabulary: DIFFERENT STUDIES HAVE ADOPTED DIFFERENT TERMINOLOGY (EITHER BURSTING OR LTS), AND REPORT SOMEWHAT DIFFERENT LAMINAR DISTRIBUTIONS, WHICH IS FURTHER COMPLICATED BY THE FACT THAT SOME STUDIES ARE IN RAT WHILE OTHERS ARE IN MOUSE
senses.evidence: Different studies have adopted different terminology (either bursting or LTS), and report somewhat different laminar distributions, which is further complicated by the fact that some studies are in rat while others are in mouse

senses.label: THE CATEGORIES ARE NOT EVEN THE SAME ACROSS SPECIES: IN RATS PV, SOM, AND CALRETININ (CR) CELLS FORM NON-OVERLAPPING CATEGORIES, WHEREAS MICE SHOW OVERLAPPING EXPRESSION OF SOM AND CR. The same three names partition one animal and not the other
senses.evidence: These categories vary across species; in rats, for example, PV, SOM, and calretinin (CR) cells form non-overlapping categories (Gonchar and Burkhalter, 1997 ; Kawaguchi and Kubota, 1997 ), whereas mice show overlapping expression of SOM and CR

senses.label: THE INCLUSION IS ONE-WAY AND THE REVIEW SAYS BOTH HALVES: ALL MARTINOTTI CELLS ARE SOM-POSITIVE, HOWEVER NOT ALL SOM-POSITIVE CELLS ARE MARTINOTTI CELLS - the exact shape a `is-a` edge needs and almost never gets
senses.head: THE INCLUSION IS ONE-WAY AND THE REVIEW SAYS BOTH HALVES: ALL MARTINOTTI CELLS ARE SOM-POSITIVE, HOWEVER NOT ALL SOM-POSITIVE CELLS ARE MARTINOTTI CELLS
senses.gloss: the exact shape a `is-a` edge needs and almost never gets
senses.evidence: All Martinotti cells are SOM-positive, however not all SOM-positive cells are Martinotti cells.

senses.label: the same one-way shape, denied in both directions for the other class: NOT ALL PV CELLS ARE FS CELLS, AND NOT ALL FS CELLS ARE PV CELLS. A molecular name and a physiological name that are used interchangeably and are not the same set
senses.evidence: However, not all PV cells are FS cells, and not all FS cells are PV cells

senses.label: THE TOOL THAT MAKES THE CLASS VISIBLE LEAKS INTO THE CLASS IT IS DEFINED AGAINST: AT LEAST ONE SOM-CRE LINE ALSO ERRONEOUSLY MARKS A SMALL SUBSET (6-10%) OF FAST SPIKING PV NEURONS
senses.evidence: It is important to note that at least one SOM-Cre line (Taniguchi et al., 2011 ; Jax Stock No. 013044) also erroneously marks a small subset (6–10%) of fast spiking PV neurons

senses.label: and the census is biased by the same tool: BECAUSE THEY LABEL ONLY SUBSETS OF SOM CELLS, ONE MUST BE CAREFUL NOT TO INFER RELATIVE PROPORTIONS OF SOM SUBTYPES FROM STUDIES USING THESE LINES
senses.evidence: But because they label only subsets of SOM cells, one must be careful not to infer relative proportions of SOM subtypes from studies using these lines.

senses.label: THE PROPERTY BELONGS TO THE INTERACTION, NOT TO THE CELL TYPE: WHETHER GAIN CONTROL IS DIVISIVE OR SUBTRACTIVE IS DYNAMIC AND STIMULUS-DEPENDENT, RATHER THAN A FIXED PROPERTY OF A GIVEN CELL TYPE. Every tag of the form `SOM provides subtractive inhibition` is therefore true only of a condition, and the condition is not in the tag
senses.evidence: This illustrates that whether gain control is divisive or subtractive is dynamic and stimulus-dependent, rather than a fixed property of a given cell type.

senses.label: and it may not belong to the interneuron at all: THESE FORMS OF GAIN CONTROL MAY NOT BE DETERMINED BY THE TYPE OF INTERNEURON, BUT RATHER BY INTRINSIC PROPERTIES OF A TARGET NEURON. The property is attributed to the wrong cell
senses.evidence: This suggests that these forms of gain control may not be determined by the type of interneuron, but rather by intrinsic properties of a target neuron

senses.label: A MEASUREMENT FLOOR THAT MANUFACTURES THE RESULT: FIRING RATES CANNOT GO BELOW ZERO (I.E., THE WATER LEVEL), WHICH HIDES THE SUBTHRESHOLD TUNING CURVE - so STRONGER SUPPRESSION OF PN SPIKING CAN NARROW TUNING CURVES, EVEN WITH PURELY DIVISIVE INHIBITION
senses.head: A MEASUREMENT FLOOR THAT MANUFACTURES THE RESULT: FIRING RATES CANNOT GO BELOW ZERO (I.E., THE WATER LEVEL), WHICH HIDES THE SUBTHRESHOLD TUNING CURVE
senses.gloss: so STRONGER SUPPRESSION OF PN SPIKING CAN NARROW TUNING CURVES, EVEN WITH PURELY DIVISIVE INHIBITION
senses.evidence: These conflicting results can best be understood in the context of the “iceberg effect,” which refers to the idea that firing rates cannot go below zero (i.e., the water level), which hides the subthreshold tuning curve.

senses.label: which the review turns into a rule about the method: INFERRING THE PRESENCE OF DIVISIVE OR SUBTRACTIVE INHIBITION FROM OPTOGENETIC MANIPULATIONS CAN BE PROBLEMATIC
senses.evidence: These studies illustrate that inferring the presence of divisive or subtractive inhibition from optogenetic manipulations can be problematic

senses.label: A CATEGORY BORROWED FROM ANOTHER CELL TYPE, WITH THE NON-IDENTITY STATED: REGULAR SPIKING AND BURSTING FIRING TYPES WERE ORIGINALLY DESCRIBED FOR CORTICAL PYRAMIDAL NEURONS, and THE FIRING PROPERTIES OF RS OR BURSTING SOM CELLS ARE ANALOGOUS BUT NOT IDENTICAL TO THOSE CLASSICALLY OBSERVED IN PYRAMIDAL NEURONS
senses.evidence: Regular spiking and bursting firing types were originally described for cortical pyramidal neurons (Connors et al., 1982 ), and it is important to note that the firing properties of RS or bursting SOM cells are analogous but not identical to those classically observed in pyramidal neurons.

senses.label: the same paper suppressing SOM and REDUCING adaptation, read the other way round: SUPPRESSION OF SOM NEURONS REDUCES STIMULUS-SPECIFIC ADAPTATION IN OTHER CORTICAL NEURONS, INCREASING PN RESPONSES TO THE FREQUENT TONE - and SOM CELLS CONTRIBUTE TO STIMULUS-SPECIFIC ADAPTATION, EVEN WHILE EXPERIENCING STIMULUS-SPECIFIC ADAPTATION THEMSELVES
senses.head: the same paper suppressing SOM and REDUCING adaptation, read the other way round: SUPPRESSION OF SOM NEURONS REDUCES STIMULUS-SPECIFIC ADAPTATION IN OTHER CORTICAL NEURONS, INCREASING PN RESPONSES TO THE FREQUENT TONE
senses.gloss: and SOM CELLS CONTRIBUTE TO STIMULUS-SPECIFIC ADAPTATION, EVEN WHILE EXPERIENCING STIMULUS-SPECIFIC ADAPTATION THEMSELVES
senses.evidence: Suppression of SOM neurons reduces stimulus-specific adaptation in other cortical neurons, increasing PN responses to the frequent tone. Thus SOM cells contribute to stimulus-specific adaptation, even while experiencing stimulus-specific adaptation themselves

senses.label: and the same cells move the opposite way in the neighboring paradigm: THIS INCREASE IN SOM RESPONSIVENESS CONTRASTS WITH THE DECREASED SOM RESPONSIVENESS DURING STIMULUS-SPECIFIC ADAPTATION
senses.evidence: Tone-evoked responses in L2/3 SOM cells are increased as both PN and PV cell responses are decreased, suggested that SOM cells mediate the habituation in other cortical neurons. This increase in SOM responsiveness contrasts with the decreased SOM responsiveness during stimulus-specific adaptation.

senses.label: THE CLASS CANNOT BE PERTURBED ALONE: IT IS VIRTUALLY IMPOSSIBLE TO PERTURB THE ACTIVITY OF THE SOM NETWORK WITHOUT CHANGING FIRING PATTERNS IN OTHER INHIBITORY NEURONS, WHICH MAY LEAD TO CONFLICTING AND MISLEADING RESULTS
senses.evidence: Lastly, high levels of interconnectivity in cortical circuits make it challenging to study the effects of only a single interneuron subtype. In particular, it is virtually impossible to perturb the activity of the SOM network without changing firing patterns in other inhibitory neurons, which may lead to conflicting and misleading results

senses.label: and the review's closing instruction to its own readers: IT IS IMPORTANT TO REMEMBER THAT SOM CELLS ARE NOT A SINGLE POPULATION, BUT RATHER CONSIST OF SEVERAL DISTINCT CLASSES OF INHIBITORY CELLS
senses.evidence: It is important to remember that SOM cells are not a single population, but rather consist of several distinct classes of inhibitory cells

senses.label: THE NAME IS ALSO A MOLECULE: SOMATOSTATIN IS NOT JUST A CELL-TYPE SPECIFIC MARKER, BUT ALSO AN INHIBITORY 14-AMINO-ACID NEUROPEPTIDE RELEASED BY THE SUBSET OF GABAERGIC NEURONS THAT EXPRESS THE SOMATOSTATIN GENE - one word doing duty as a label and as a substance
senses.head: THE NAME IS ALSO A MOLECULE: SOMATOSTATIN IS NOT JUST A CELL-TYPE SPECIFIC MARKER, BUT ALSO AN INHIBITORY 14-AMINO-ACID NEUROPEPTIDE RELEASED BY THE SUBSET OF GABAERGIC NEURONS THAT EXPRESS THE SOMATOSTATIN GENE
senses.gloss: one word doing duty as a label and as a substance
senses.evidence: Somatostatin is not just a cell-type specific marker, but also an inhibitory 14-amino-acid neuropeptide released by the subset of GABAergic neurons that express the somatostatin gene.

senses.label: and what that substance does where the review is set is not known: THE CELLULAR AND SYNAPTIC EFFECTS OF SOM RELEASE IN CORTEX HAVE NOT BEEN STUDIED
senses.evidence: The cellular and synaptic effects of SOM release in cortex have not been studied.

senses.label: the same class behaving oppositely in one sensory system: IN BARREL CORTEX SOM CELLS ARE SUPPRESSED DURING STIMULUS PRESENTATION, AND THUS ARE ANTI-CORRELATED WITH NETWORK ACTIVITY, A FEATURE WHICH HAS NOT BEEN OBSERVED IN OTHER SENSORY REGIONS
senses.evidence: Interestingly, in barrel cortex SOM cells are suppressed during stimulus presentation, and thus are anti-correlated with network activity, a feature which has not been observed in other sensory regions

senses.label: multiculturalism against assimilation and colorblindness - THREE DIVERSITY MODELS ON ONE AXIS, and the axis is stated: whether cultural difference is APPRECIATED or IGNORED. Colorblindness and assimilation are put on the same side, which is a grouping this literature does not always make
senses.head: multiculturalism against assimilation and colorblindness
senses.gloss: THREE DIVERSITY MODELS ON ONE AXIS, and the axis is stated: whether cultural difference is APPRECIATED or IGNORED. Colorblindness and assimilation are put on the same side, which is a grouping this literature does not always make
senses.evidence: Models of Cultural Diversity Multiculturalism emphasizes the appreciation of different cultural values, traditions, and lifestyles, in contrast to colorblindness or assimilation, which reflect a preference toward ignoring cultural differences

senses.label: social distance, as measured here - a construct defined by the EXTENT of contact refused, from marriage down to co-residence in a city. The scale is the definition, which is what makes `prejudice` operational in this design
senses.head: social distance, as measured here
senses.gloss: a construct defined by the EXTENT of contact refused, from marriage down to co-residence in a city. The scale is the definition, which is what makes `prejudice` operational in this design
senses.evidence: Desire to keep one’s social distance from outgroups (Bogardus, 1925, 1947), ranging from being unwilling to marry an outgroup member up to even being unwilling to live in the same city

senses.label: the prime, in this study - not a word list or a photograph but A DESCRIPTION OF THE READER'S OWN COUNTRY: a passage about how China handles diversity, read by Hong Kong students who are both minority and majority culture members. The manipulation is a national self-description
senses.head: the prime, in this study
senses.gloss: not a word list or a photograph but A DESCRIPTION OF THE READER'S OWN COUNTRY: a passage about how China handles diversity, read by Hong Kong students who are both minority and majority culture members. The manipulation is a national self-description
senses.evidence: Results show new evidence of the importance of emotion in how non-immigrant regional groups, who are both minority and majority culture members, react to different diversity models

senses.label: THE SAME CONTRAST GETS A DIFFERENT NAME UNDER A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT: deviant minus standard is called mismatch negativity in the electrophysiology and mismatch response in the calcium imaging, because the indicator's responses go up rather than down and decay slowly
senses.evidence: The comparison between standard and deviant conditions for the calcium imaging data was called mismatch response (MMR) due to the GCaMP protein exhibiting primarily positive increases in activity and its slow decay kinetics.

senses.label: and the analysis window is set by the indicator rather than by the phenomenon - 300 to 1,500 ms is chosen because that is when the calcium signal has decayed, not because that is when the process happens
senses.head: and the analysis window is set by the indicator rather than by the phenomenon
senses.gloss: 300 to 1,500 ms is chosen because that is when the calcium signal has decayed, not because that is when the process happens
senses.evidence: Due to the slow decay kinetics of the GCaMP6f fluorescence indicator, it is difficult to interpret when certain processes are occurring during periods of neural activity. Accordingly, we chose the period of time that calcium responses largely decayed back to baseline (from 300 to 1,500 ms relative to stimulus onset) when performing statistics or averaging across the epoch of time related to stimulus response.

senses.label: A THIRD CONDITION IS BUILT TO CONTAIN NEITHER RIVAL: the many-standards block is rare like the deviant and unrepeated like nothing else, so it elicits neither adaptation nor surprise and lets the difference be split in two
senses.evidence: A third block’s (many-standards control block) stimuli consisted of 10 equiprobable drifting gratings of different motion directions (same structure and stimuli as the initial tuning curve session); stimuli presented in this third condition served as controls that do not elicit adaptation effects of the standard condition or surprise effects like the deviant condition.

senses.label: and the same two stimuli swap roles between blocks, which removes stimulus preference as a confound by construction rather than by correction
senses.evidence: In one block (oddball A), the two best responsive stimuli from the first session were chosen to be presented in either the standard (90% of trials) or deviant (10% of trials) condition (ie. stimulus A was the deviant and B was the standard). In another block (oddball B), the same two stimuli were used but the conditions were switched (ie. stimulus B was the deviant and A was the standard). The reason for presenting both of these blocks is to be able to compare the same stimulus presented in different conditions, thus removing the confounding factor of stimulus-preference when examining neural activity.

senses.label: THE NULL IS CONSTRUCTED FROM WHAT THE ARTEFACT CANNOT DO: shuffling trial labels within a block preserves every block-to-block difference and destroys only the condition difference, and that shuffle is subtracted region by region
senses.evidence: A concern arises when comparing activity between conditions for a certain stimulus: observed differences could arise and be confounded by block-to-block differences in baseline fluorescence. To account for this concern, we baseline corrected all time-courses on a trial level. Further, when calculating the condition contrasts, we performed a trial condition shuffle control. This first involved computing trial-averaged activity with trial conditions shuffled within each block (effectively preserving block-to-block differences in activity, while eliminating condition-dependent differences). The condition contrast was then computed (MMR or DD). Finally, trial-averaged shuffle data were subtracted from trial condition-intact data on a ROI-by-ROI basis.

senses.label: THE CONTROL AREA IS SPOILED BY THE SELECTION PROCEDURE: the stimuli were chosen to drive parietal cortex, so a null in visual cortex says nothing, and the paper says so
senses.evidence: MMN was not found to be significant for either stimuli in the VC ERPs (Supplementary Fig. 3 ). Although the difference between standard and deviant responses for Stimulus A is trending (t(6) = 2.36, p = 0.056), these results are difficult to interpret since the oddball stimuli were chosen based on PPC preference.

senses.label: AND THE POPULATION AVERAGE SHOWS NOTHING: multi-unit firing gave no difference across conditions, with the signal proposed to live in select cells invisible to a neuron-averaged rate
senses.evidence: Furthermore, we found no differences in spiking magnitude across oddball conditions (Supplementary Fig. 4 ). It is possible, at least for PPC, that the MMN is a specialized signal present in select cells and is not immediately apparent in the general neuron-averaged multi-unit firing rate.

senses.label: the negative result is defended rather than buried: the absence of deviance detection is named as something that might be read as diminishing the study, and then turned into the contribution
senses.evidence: Further, it may be construed that the lack of deviance detection in our results diminishes the significance of our study; however, by demonstrating that stimulus-dependent adaptation manifests across sparsely encoded cells, our findings build upon several seminal works that highlight the contribution of adaptation to MMN 16 , 17 , 59 . Our novel contribution to this adaptation hypothesis is that this attenuation of the ERP obligatory component may depend on single neuron stimulus preference.

senses.label: and an internal tension is stated outright - stimulus-specific mismatch responses but adaptation for both stimuli - with a proposed resolution offered as a proposal
senses.head: and an internal tension is stated outright
senses.gloss: stimulus-specific mismatch responses but adaptation for both stimuli - with a proposed resolution offered as a proposal
senses.evidence: Finally, it is important to reconcile that we observed stimulus-specific MMR in the calcium imaging results, but SSA for both stimuli. We believe the stimulus-specific component of the MMR could arise from suppression of activity in the opponent stimulus’ deviant condition. Such a phenomenon could serve as a signal-to-noise amplification mechanism for stimulus presentation frequency differentiation in the local PPC circuitry.

senses.label: THE STIMULUS CARRIES TWO FEATURES AT ONCE: opposing directions share an orientation, and orientation does not change between conditions, so the missing effect for one stimulus may be about which feature the cells are tracking
senses.evidence: Finally, it is possible to explain the stimulus-specific MMN results in the context of the multiplexing of stimulus direction and orientation. Stimuli with opposing directions share the same orientation and therefore with the stimuli chosen in our study, PPC neurons may contend with both orientation and direction information. This is particularly important for the opponent stimulus where PPC activity could be dominated more by the stimulus orientation rather than direction. Since orientation remains invariant across standard and deviant conditions, this may explain the lack of MMN for the opponent stimulus.

senses.label: THE PRIMING ARM MAY HAVE STOPPED BEING A NUDGE, AND THE AUTHORS SAY SO IN THEIR OWN DISCUSSION: the green ambience `could lead to an activation of a REFLECTIVE decision making, promoting a healthy-eater self-schema of food choice, HENCE NOT BE AN AUTOMATIC PROCESS NUDGE, BUT A REFLECTIVE.` The room was meant to work below awareness; it may instead have reminded people that they are the kind of person who eats well. **The intervention had an effect and the CATEGORY it was meant to demonstrate did not survive it** - which is a different kind of negative result from a null, and one a corpus that records only effect sizes cannot hold
senses.head: THE PRIMING ARM MAY HAVE STOPPED BEING A NUDGE, AND THE AUTHORS SAY SO IN THEIR OWN DISCUSSION: the green ambience `could lead to an activation of a REFLECTIVE decision making, promoting a healthy-eater self-schema of food choice, HENCE NOT BE AN AUTOMATIC PROCESS NUDGE, BUT A REFLECTIVE.` The room was meant to work below awareness; it may instead have reminded people that they are the kind of person who eats well. **The intervention had an effect and the CATEGORY it was meant to demonstrate did not survive it**
senses.gloss: which is a different kind of negative result from a null, and one a corpus that records only effect sizes cannot hold
senses.evidence: This could lead to an activation of a reflective decision making, promoting a healthy-eater self-schema of food choice [40], hence not be an automatic process nudge, but a reflective

senses.label: AND THEY SAY THEY CANNOT TELL WHICH IT WAS: `However, this study DID NOT MEASURE the participants' level of health-schematic NOR TO WHAT EXTENT THEIR FOOD CHOICE WAS REFLECTIVE OR NOT.` The distinction that decides whether the finding is a nudge result or its opposite was not measured. Stated plainly, immediately after the interpretation that depends on it, rather than left for a reader to notice
senses.evidence: However, this study did not measure the participants’ level of health-schematic nor to what extent their food choice was reflective or not

senses.label: THE DEFINITION OF A NUDGE FORBIDS ITS OWN MANIPULATION CHECK, which is the sharpest thing in this paper. The variety arm had to leave the ACTUAL variety unchanged `IN ORDER TO BE CONSISTENT WITH THE DEFINITION OF A NUDGE` - and then: `ASKING THE PARTICIPANTS of their perception of the vegetable variety WOULD REQUIRE THEM TO EMBARK IN REFLECTIVE DECISION-MAKING, THUS LOSING THE INTENDED IDEA OF NUDGING their food choice.` **You cannot ask whether it worked without destroying the thing you are asking about.** The definition does not merely describe the intervention; it rules out the measurement that would verify it
senses.head: THE DEFINITION OF A NUDGE FORBIDS ITS OWN MANIPULATION CHECK, which is the sharpest thing in this paper. The variety arm had to leave the ACTUAL variety unchanged `IN ORDER TO BE CONSISTENT WITH THE DEFINITION OF A NUDGE`
senses.gloss: and then: `ASKING THE PARTICIPANTS of their perception of the vegetable variety WOULD REQUIRE THEM TO EMBARK IN REFLECTIVE DECISION-MAKING, THUS LOSING THE INTENDED IDEA OF NUDGING their food choice.` **You cannot ask whether it worked without destroying the thing you are asking about.** The definition does not merely describe the intervention; it rules out the measurement that would verify it
senses.evidence: Asking the participants of their perception of the vegetable variety would require them to embark in reflective decision-making thus losing the intended idea of nudging their food choice

senses.label: THE ARM THAT `WORKED` MOVED THE WRONG VARIABLE, TWICE OVER. Priming did not raise vegetable intake - it `significantly DECREASED THE CONSUMPTION OF CHILLI CON CARNE`. And the variety arm `decreased the self-served amount of meat and total energy, BUT THE TOTAL INTAKE OF VEGETABLES WAS NOT INCREASED AS HYPOTHESISED`. Two of three interventions produced a healthier meal by SUBTRACTION rather than by the addition they were designed to cause, so a summary reporting `nudges promoted healthier meal composition` is true and tells a reader the opposite of what happened
senses.head: THE ARM THAT `WORKED` MOVED THE WRONG VARIABLE, TWICE OVER. Priming did not raise vegetable intake
senses.gloss: it `significantly DECREASED THE CONSUMPTION OF CHILLI CON CARNE`. And the variety arm `decreased the self-served amount of meat and total energy, BUT THE TOTAL INTAKE OF VEGETABLES WAS NOT INCREASED AS HYPOTHESISED`. Two of three interventions produced a healthier meal by SUBTRACTION rather than by the addition they were designed to cause, so a summary reporting `nudges promoted healthier meal composition` is true and tells a reader the opposite of what happened
senses.evidence: The experiment of increasing the visual perceived variety decreased the self-served amount of meat and total energy, but the total intake of vegetables was not increased as hypothesised

senses.label: A CONFOUND NAMED AT THE CONCEPTUAL LEVEL RATHER THAN THE STATISTICAL ONE: `From a conceptual level an important concern to address is that DEFAULT AND VARIETY CONDITIONS ALSO DIFFER IN THE EASINESS TO REACH THE VEGETABLES.` In the default arm people grasped a pre-packed box; in the variety arm they served themselves. So the two conditions differ in effort as well as in the thing being manipulated, and no statistic in the paper separates them. The authors raise it against their own comparison
senses.evidence: From a conceptual level an important concern to address is that default and variety conditions also differ in the easiness to reach the vegetables

senses.label: **THE DEFINITION IS THE RARE THING HERE.** `Priming, a change in the mental processing of a stimulus as a result of prior encounter with a RELATED stimulus, has been observed repeatedly and studied extensively in humans.` Most of this corpus assumes the term and argues about mechanisms - meyer1971 contains the word zero times, neely1977 uses it only in its title and running headers. **A paper extending a concept to a new species has to say what the concept is**, and that pressure is why the definition exists at all
senses.head: **THE DEFINITION IS THE RARE THING HERE.** `Priming, a change in the mental processing of a stimulus as a result of prior encounter with a RELATED stimulus, has been observed repeatedly and studied extensively in humans.` Most of this corpus assumes the term and argues about mechanisms
senses.gloss: meyer1971 contains the word zero times, neely1977 uses it only in its title and running headers. **A paper extending a concept to a new species has to say what the concept is**, and that pressure is why the definition exists at all
senses.evidence: Priming, a change in the mental processing of a stimulus as a result of prior encounter with a related stimulus, has been observed repeatedly and studied extensively in humans.

senses.label: **AND THE CROSS-SPECIES RESULT IS A DIFFERENCE, NOT A CONFIRMATION:** `First, in mice, the priming effect is in SUCCESS RATES and not in response times, whereas in humans, the priming effect is BOTH in success rates and response times.` So it is not that the two species use different measures - **humans show the effect in both channels and mice show it in only one.** A weaker paper would have reported that priming generalises to mice; this one reports which measure it lands in and that the human pattern is strictly larger. The concept survives the species change and its operationalisation does not, which is exactly the case a controlled vocabulary handles worst: both would be tagged `priming effect` and the tag would hide the disagreement. **I first quoted the figure caption for this, which says only `in humans, the typical priming effect is in response time` - the looser claim. The discussion is more precise than the caption and I had taken the caption as the paper's position**
senses.head: **AND THE CROSS-SPECIES RESULT IS A DIFFERENCE, NOT A CONFIRMATION:** `First, in mice, the priming effect is in SUCCESS RATES and not in response times, whereas in humans, the priming effect is BOTH in success rates and response times.` So it is not that the two species use different measures
senses.gloss: **humans show the effect in both channels and mice show it in only one.** A weaker paper would have reported that priming generalises to mice; this one reports which measure it lands in and that the human pattern is strictly larger. The concept survives the species change and its operationalisation does not, which is exactly the case a controlled vocabulary handles worst: both would be tagged `priming effect` and the tag would hide the disagreement. **I first quoted the figure caption for this, which says only `in humans, the typical priming effect is in response time` - the looser claim. The discussion is more precise than the caption and I had taken the caption as the paper's position**
senses.evidence: First, in mice, the priming effect is in success rates and not in response times, whereas in humans, the priming effect is both in success rates and response times.

senses.label: **THE MECHANISM CLAIM IS ASYMMETRIC AND THE PAPER SAYS SO RATHER THAN LETTING THE MEASURE IMPLY IT:** `the addition of INCONGRUENT prime stimuli reduces success rate MORE THAN congruent prime stimuli, suggesting a cognitive mechanism based on DIFFERENTIAL INTERFERENCE.` Both prime types cost performance against unprimed trials; the incongruent ones cost more. So the priming effect here is **a difference between two costs, not a benefit over a baseline** - and the standard congruent-minus-incongruent measure is identical in both stories while reading naturally as facilitation.
