senses.label: autonomy - IN THIS PAPER A REAL AND MEASURED FREEDOM THAT DOES NOT IMPLY GOOD WORK. 72% could choose the order of tasks and 74% their methods, and the same workers report overwork, sleep deprivation and exhaustion. The paper's whole argument is that autonomy and job quality come apart, so reading `autonomy` as a job-quality outcome inverts the finding
senses.head: autonomy
senses.gloss: IN THIS PAPER A REAL AND MEASURED FREEDOM THAT DOES NOT IMPLY GOOD WORK. 72% could choose the order of tasks and 74% their methods, and the same workers report overwork, sleep deprivation and exhaustion. The paper's whole argument is that autonomy and job quality come apart, so reading `autonomy` as a job-quality outcome inverts the finding
senses.evidence: This is echoed in our survey, where 72% of respondents felt able to choose and change the order in which they undertook online tasks, and 74% were able to choose or change their methods of work.

senses.label: algorithmic control - CONTROL EXERCISED AT THE END OF THE LABOUR PROCESS RATHER THAN DURING IT. That single structural fact generates the whole pattern: because only the output is judged, the worker is free in how they work, and because the rating governs future work, the freedom is unusable
senses.head: algorithmic control
senses.gloss: CONTROL EXERCISED AT THE END OF THE LABOUR PROCESS RATHER THAN DURING IT. That single structural fact generates the whole pattern: because only the output is judged, the worker is free in how they work, and because the rating governs future work, the freedom is unusable
senses.evidence: What is notable about this algorithmic system of control in terms of job quality, compared to Taylorist forms of informational control, is that control operated at the end of the labour process rather than during it.

senses.label: algorithmic management - NOT SUPERVISION BY MACHINE BUT CUSTOMER MANAGEMENT EXTENDED: the client is placed in the management circuit, and the platform's ranking turns their rating into a sanction. The controller is another user, not an algorithm with a policy
senses.head: algorithmic management
senses.gloss: NOT SUPERVISION BY MACHINE BUT CUSTOMER MANAGEMENT EXTENDED: the client is placed in the management circuit, and the platform's ranking turns their rating into a sanction. The controller is another user, not an algorithm with a policy
senses.evidence: Algorithmic management is an extension of ‘customer management’ strategies, which entails positioning customers ‘as agents in the management circuit’, so that ‘customers, rather than managers, are \[…\] the ones who must be pleased, whose orders must be followed, whose ideas, whims and desires appear to dictate how work is performed’

senses.label: platform reputation - AN INDIVIDUAL RESOURCE IN THE LABOUR MARKET, alongside skills, rather than a signal about past work. It is what the paper means by reputation having `symbolic power`: it is held by the worker, cannot be transferred between platforms, and determines what work is reachable at all
senses.head: platform reputation
senses.gloss: AN INDIVIDUAL RESOURCE IN THE LABOUR MARKET, alongside skills, rather than a signal about past work. It is what the paper means by reputation having `symbolic power`: it is held by the worker, cannot be transferred between platforms, and determines what work is reachable at all
senses.evidence: In the case of remote gig work, the individual resources that we find to be most important are _skills_ and _platform reputation_. Workers lacking these individual resources suffered from low incomes and insecurity.

senses.label: blinding - IN THIS TRIAL A MATTER OF DEGREE THAT THE AUTHORS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Every participant was told psilocybin would be given on each session, so the comparison is high dose against a very low dose, not against an inert placebo. The paper's own verdict is `SOME protection`, not blinding
senses.head: blinding
senses.gloss: IN THIS TRIAL A MATTER OF DEGREE THAT THE AUTHORS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Every participant was told psilocybin would be given on each session, so the comparison is high dose against a very low dose, not against an inert placebo. The paper's own verdict is `SOME protection`, not blinding
senses.evidence: Overall, we conclude that the blinding procedures provided some protection against a priori monitor expectancy strongly determining outcomes of the psilocybin dose manipulation.

senses.label: very low dose - A PLACEBO-LIKE DOSE AND NOT A PLACEBO, and the authors say the difference matters: 1 mg/70 kg was assumed largely inactive and they state that some pharmacological activity cannot be ruled out, and that a far lower dose would have been preferable
senses.head: very low dose
senses.gloss: A PLACEBO-LIKE DOSE AND NOT A PLACEBO, and the authors say the difference matters: 1 mg/70 kg was assumed largely inactive and they state that some pharmacological activity cannot be ruled out, and that a far lower dose would have been preferable
senses.evidence: Although it was assumed that 1 mg/70 kg would be largely pharmacologically inactive, some pharmacological activity of this dose cannot be ruled out entirely.

senses.label: mystical-type experience - USED HERE AS A MEASURED MEDIATOR ON SESSION DAY, not as a description of how the drug felt. It is the variable through which dose reaches therapeutic outcome, which makes it part of the causal claim rather than a side observation
senses.head: mystical-type experience
senses.gloss: USED HERE AS A MEASURED MEDIATOR ON SESSION DAY, not as a description of how the drug felt. It is the variable through which dose reaches therapeutic outcome, which makes it part of the causal claim rather than a side observation
senses.evidence: Mystical-type psilocybin experience on session day mediated the effect of psilocybin dose on therapeutic outcomes.

senses.label: placebo - IN THIS TRIAL NIACIN, AN ACTIVE PLACEBO CHOSEN TO PRODUCE A NOTICEABLE SOMATIC EFFECT, not an inert capsule. The companion trial in the same issue used a very low dose of psilocybin instead. Two teams reached the same result through two different solutions to the same problem - that an inert placebo is unblindable against a psychedelic
senses.head: placebo
senses.gloss: IN THIS TRIAL NIACIN, AN ACTIVE PLACEBO CHOSEN TO PRODUCE A NOTICEABLE SOMATIC EFFECT, not an inert capsule. The companion trial in the same issue used a very low dose of psilocybin instead. Two teams reached the same result through two different solutions to the same problem - that an inert placebo is unblindable against a psychedelic
senses.evidence: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial, 29 patients with cancer-related anxiety and depression were randomly assigned and received treatment with single-dose psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or niacin, both in conjunction with psychotherapy.

senses.label: mystical experience - A MEASURED MEDIATOR AND EXPLICITLY NOT THE ONLY ONE: the authors say it is `likely to be one of several mediators`, which is a weaker and more careful claim than the abstract's `mediated the therapeutic effect`
senses.head: mystical experience
senses.gloss: A MEASURED MEDIATOR AND EXPLICITLY NOT THE ONLY ONE: the authors say it is `likely to be one of several mediators`, which is a weaker and more careful claim than the abstract's `mediated the therapeutic effect`
senses.evidence: The mystical experience is likely to be one of several mediators that transmit the effect of psilocybin to changes in anxiety and/or depression.

senses.label: difficult experience - NOT AN ADVERSE EVENT IN THIS FRAMEWORK. Transient anxiety or paranoia is to be monitored and managed, and is read as part of the therapeutic process rather than as harm, which changes what the safety numbers of a psychedelic trial mean
senses.head: difficult experience
senses.gloss: NOT AN ADVERSE EVENT IN THIS FRAMEWORK. Transient anxiety or paranoia is to be monitored and managed, and is read as part of the therapeutic process rather than as harm, which changes what the safety numbers of a psychedelic trial mean
senses.evidence: Difficult experiences are not necessarily pathological and can be understood as part of the therapeutic process (e.g. working through cancer-related psychological or existential distress through challenging encounters or emotionally charged confrontations with cancer-related fearful imagery or symbolism)

senses.label: psychological impact - IN THIS PAPER A SCORE ON THE IMPACT OF EVENT SCALE-REVISED, an instrument built for post-traumatic stress reactions to a specific event, and NOT a clinical assessment. The authors say so themselves: self-reported levels may not align with assessment by mental health professionals
senses.head: psychological impact
senses.gloss: IN THIS PAPER A SCORE ON THE IMPACT OF EVENT SCALE-REVISED, an instrument built for post-traumatic stress reactions to a specific event, and NOT a clinical assessment. The authors say so themselves: self-reported levels may not align with assessment by mental health professionals
senses.evidence: Another limitation is that self-reported levels of psychological impact, anxiety, depression and stress may not always be aligned with assessment by mental health professionals.

senses.label: associated with - THE PAPER'S OWN CEILING AND IT KEEPS TO IT EVERYWHERE. The design is cross-sectional and the analysis is UNIVARIATE linear regression, so nothing here is adjusted for anything else and no temporal order is observed. `Female gender ... associated with a greater psychological impact` is a difference between groups measured on one day
senses.head: associated with
senses.gloss: THE PAPER'S OWN CEILING AND IT KEEPS TO IT EVERYWHERE. The design is cross-sectional and the analysis is UNIVARIATE linear regression, so nothing here is adjusted for anything else and no temporal order is observed. `Female gender ... associated with a greater psychological impact` is a difference between groups measured on one day
senses.evidence: We used linear regressions to calculate the univariate associations between sociodemographic characteristics, physical symptom and health service utilization variables, contact history variables, knowledge and concern variables, precautionary measure variables, additional health information variables, and the IES-S score as well as the subscales of the DASS.

senses.label: the general public - RECRUITED FROM UNIVERSITY STUDENTS OUTWARD, which the authors name as oversampling one network of peers. The sample is 1,210 people across 194 cities and it is explicitly not a picture of the general population
senses.head: the general public
senses.gloss: RECRUITED FROM UNIVERSITY STUDENTS OUTWARD, which the authors name as oversampling one network of peers. The sample is 1,210 people across 194 cities and it is explicitly not a picture of the general population
senses.evidence: There was an oversampling of a particular network of peers (e.g., students), leading to selection bias. As a result, the conclusion was less generalizable to the entire population, particularly less educated people.

senses.label: food waste - THE PAPER ENUMERATES THREE COMPETING DEFINITIONS AND SAYS WHICH IT USES, which is rare enough to be the reason this record is worth holding. (1) FAO 1981: wholesome edible material intended for human consumption, discarded, lost, degraded or eaten by pests anywhere in the chain. (2) Stuart 2009: as (1) PLUS edible material fed to animals or diverted as a processing by-product. (3) Smil 2004: as (1) and (2) PLUS OVER-NUTRITION - the gap between energy consumed and energy needed. The paper adopts the first two and states that the second is only usable where nutritional data on animal feed exist
senses.head: food waste
senses.gloss: THE PAPER ENUMERATES THREE COMPETING DEFINITIONS AND SAYS WHICH IT USES, which is rare enough to be the reason this record is worth holding. (1) FAO 1981: wholesome edible material intended for human consumption, discarded, lost, degraded or eaten by pests anywhere in the chain. (2) Stuart 2009: as (1) PLUS edible material fed to animals or diverted as a processing by-product. (3) Smil 2004: as (1) and (2) PLUS OVER-NUTRITION - the gap between energy consumed and energy needed. The paper adopts the first two and states that the second is only usable where nutritional data on animal feed exist
senses.evidence: As definitions (1) and (2) but including over-nutrition—the gap between the energy value of _consumed_ food _per capita_ and the energy value of food _needed per capita_ (Smil 2004 _a_).

senses.label: food waste vs food LOSS - NOT SYNONYMS AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WHERE THE REMEDY GOES. `Food loss` is used post-harvest and names a decrease in quantity or quality; `food waste` is used at the consumer end and relates to behaviour. Losses want investment in infrastructure, waste wants behavioural change - so which word a study uses commits it to a class of intervention
senses.head: food waste vs food LOSS
senses.gloss: NOT SYNONYMS AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WHERE THE REMEDY GOES. `Food loss` is used post-harvest and names a decrease in quantity or quality; `food waste` is used at the consumer end and relates to behaviour. Losses want investment in infrastructure, waste wants behavioural change - so which word a study uses commits it to a class of intervention
senses.evidence: Within the literature, food waste post-harvest is likely to be referred to as ‘food losses’ and ‘spoilage’. Food loss refers to the decrease in food quantity or quality, which makes it unfit for human consumption (Grolleaud 2002). At later stages of the FSC, the term food waste is applied and generally relates to behavioural issues. Food losses/spoilage, conversely, relate to systems that require investment in infrastructure.

senses.label: household food waste - A THREE-WAY CLASSIFICATION, `avoidable`, `possibly avoidable` and `unavoidable`, and a bounded scope: it counts only what is disposed of through household streams, which EXCLUDES food eaten on-the-go, at work or in catering. A household figure is therefore not a per-person figure
senses.head: household food waste
senses.gloss: A THREE-WAY CLASSIFICATION, `avoidable`, `possibly avoidable` and `unavoidable`, and a bounded scope: it counts only what is disposed of through household streams, which EXCLUDES food eaten on-the-go, at work or in catering. A household figure is therefore not a per-person figure
senses.evidence: Wherever possible, the distinction is made between three classifications of household food waste (figure 4): ‘avoidable’, ‘possibly avoidable’ and ‘unavoidable’.

senses.label: the `half of all food is wasted` figure - THE MOST QUOTED ESTIMATE IN THE FIELD AND THE PAPER TREATS IT AS UNSCRUTINISABLE. It is cited here as the received claim being examined, not as a finding of this review, and the review's own conclusion is that the range 10-50% traces back to one limited set of 1970s-80s fieldwork
senses.head: the `half of all food is wasted` figure
senses.gloss: THE MOST QUOTED ESTIMATE IN THE FIELD AND THE PAPER TREATS IT AS UNSCRUTINISABLE. It is cited here as the received claim being examined, not as a finding of this review, and the review's own conclusion is that the range 10-50% traces back to one limited set of 1970s-80s fieldwork
senses.evidence: The most often quoted estimate is that ‘as much as half of all food grown is lost or wasted before and after it reaches the consumer’ (Lundqvist _et al_. 2008).

senses.label: the war's `impact` on food security - THE PAPER SEPARATES TWO KINDS AND THE DISTINCTION IS ITS STRUCTURE. IMMEDIATE impacts are physical and observed: exports stopped, ports blocked, farmers conscripted. INDIRECT ones are market-mediated and projected: fertilizer prices, export restrictions, panic buying. A reader who collapses them reads observations and forecasts as one kind of claim
senses.head: the war's `impact` on food security
senses.gloss: THE PAPER SEPARATES TWO KINDS AND THE DISTINCTION IS ITS STRUCTURE. IMMEDIATE impacts are physical and observed: exports stopped, ports blocked, farmers conscripted. INDIRECT ones are market-mediated and projected: fertilizer prices, export restrictions, panic buying. A reader who collapses them reads observations and forecasts as one kind of claim
senses.evidence: The paper highlights that the war resulted in immediate and far-reaching cascading consequences on global food security: Ukrainian exports have stopped, conscription and population displacement have caused labor shortages, access to fertilizers is restricted, and future harvests are uncertain.

senses.label: the war as CAUSE - THE PAPER'S OWN THESIS IS THAT IT IS NOT THE CAUSE, IT IS THE TRIGGER. The consequences are said to be `exacerbated by a variety of underlying rigidities, vulnerabilities, and inefficiencies in global food systems`, which makes the war a stressor on a system already fragile - and it is why the conclusion is about food-system reform rather than about the war
senses.head: the war as CAUSE
senses.gloss: THE PAPER'S OWN THESIS IS THAT IT IS NOT THE CAUSE, IT IS THE TRIGGER. The consequences are said to be `exacerbated by a variety of underlying rigidities, vulnerabilities, and inefficiencies in global food systems`, which makes the war a stressor on a system already fragile - and it is why the conclusion is about food-system reform rather than about the war
senses.evidence: However, the consequences of the war on food security are being exacerbated by a variety of underlying rigidities, vulnerabilities, and inefficiencies in global food systems.

senses.label: vulnerability - DEFINED HERE BY IMPORT CONCENTRATION, not by poverty or by proximity to the war: over 30 countries take at least 30% of their wheat from Russia and Ukraine and at least 20 take more than 50%. That is what makes the effects land `far from the initial occurrence`
senses.head: vulnerability
senses.gloss: DEFINED HERE BY IMPORT CONCENTRATION, not by poverty or by proximity to the war: over 30 countries take at least 30% of their wheat from Russia and Ukraine and at least 20 take more than 50%. That is what makes the effects land `far from the initial occurrence`
senses.evidence: Indeed, over 30 countries rely on Russia and Ukraine for at least 30% of their wheat imports, while at least 20 countries rely on those two countries for more than 50% of their wheat imports, making them very sensitive to price shocks and/or supply shortages

senses.label: feature - THREE NAMES FOR ONE THING, SAID IN ONE SENTENCE: `a set of attributes, ALSO KNOWN AS features or variables`. The corpus holds `variables` as a content_tags layer and `features` as a concept on other records, and this is the paper that says they are the same object seen from statistics, from machine learning and from experimental design
senses.head: feature
senses.gloss: THREE NAMES FOR ONE THING, SAID IN ONE SENTENCE: `a set of attributes, ALSO KNOWN AS features or variables`. The corpus holds `variables` as a content_tags layer and `features` as a concept on other records, and this is the paper that says they are the same object seen from statistics, from machine learning and from experimental design
senses.evidence: Usually, an individual example is described by a set of attributes, also known as features or variables.

senses.label: supervised / unsupervised - THE DIVIDING LINE IS THE LEARNING SIGNAL, NOT THE ALGORITHM. Supervised means inputs arrive with their outputs and the goal is a rule mapping one to the other; unsupervised means there is NO DISTINCTION BETWEEN TRAINING AND TEST SETS at all, which is a stronger statement than `unlabelled data` and is what makes the two families incomparable on accuracy
senses.head: supervised / unsupervised
senses.gloss: THE DIVIDING LINE IS THE LEARNING SIGNAL, NOT THE ALGORITHM. Supervised means inputs arrive with their outputs and the goal is a rule mapping one to the other; unsupervised means there is NO DISTINCTION BETWEEN TRAINING AND TEST SETS at all, which is a stronger statement than `unlabelled data` and is what makes the two families incomparable on accuracy
senses.evidence: In unsupervised learning, however, there is no distinction between training and test sets with data being unlabeled. The learner processes input data with the goal of discovering hidden patterns.

senses.label: reinforcement learning - PLACED HERE AS A PARTIAL CASE OF SUPERVISION rather than a third family: inputs partially available, some target outputs missing or given only as feedback to actions in a dynamic environment. Other papers in this corpus treat it as a peer of the other two, and the disagreement is about what the taxonomy is FOR
senses.head: reinforcement learning
senses.gloss: PLACED HERE AS A PARTIAL CASE OF SUPERVISION rather than a third family: inputs partially available, some target outputs missing or given only as feedback to actions in a dynamic environment. Other papers in this corpus treat it as a peer of the other two, and the disagreement is about what the taxonomy is FOR
senses.evidence: In some cases, inputs can be only partially available with some of the target outputs missing or given only as feedback to the actions in a dynamic environment (reinforcement learning).

senses.label: this paper's `review` - A NARRATIVE REVIEW WITH A SEARCH ENGINE LIST AND NO INCLUSION CRITERIA. Scopus, ScienceDirect and PubMed are named; no keywords, no screening rule and no exclusion count are given, and 40 is reported as a result. Its percentages are therefore descriptive of a corpus assembled by unstated means
senses.head: this paper's `review`
senses.gloss: A NARRATIVE REVIEW WITH A SEARCH ENGINE LIST AND NO INCLUSION CRITERIA. Scopus, ScienceDirect and PubMed are named; no keywords, no screening rule and no exclusion count are given, and 40 is reported as a result. Its percentages are therefore descriptive of a corpus assembled by unstated means
senses.evidence: The search engines implemented were Scopus, ScienceDirect and PubMed. The selected articles regard works presented solely in journal papers.

senses.label: the 30,880 images - NOT 30,880 PLANTS. Just over 3,000 ORIGINAL images were collected and extended to more than 30,000 by affine, perspective and rotation transforms. Every accuracy figure in the paper rests on a dataset that is roughly 90% transformed copies, and the paper says so plainly
senses.head: the 30,880 images
senses.gloss: NOT 30,880 PLANTS. Just over 3,000 ORIGINAL images were collected and extended to more than 30,000 by affine, perspective and rotation transforms. Every accuracy figure in the paper rests on a dataset that is roughly 90% transformed copies, and the paper says so plainly
senses.evidence: New plant disease image database was created, containing more than 3,000 original images taken from the available Internet sources and extended to more than 30,000 using appropriate transformations.

senses.label: validation here is 2,589 ORIGINAL images against training on the full 30,880 - so the held-out set is untransformed while training is mostly augmented. THE PAPER DOES NOT STATE WHETHER AUGMENTED COPIES OF THE VALIDATION ORIGINALS WERE EXCLUDED FROM TRAINING, which is the question a reader of the 96.3% would want answered and it is an ABSENCE, not a stated flaw
senses.head: validation here is 2,589 ORIGINAL images against training on the full 30,880
senses.gloss: so the held-out set is untransformed while training is mostly augmented. THE PAPER DOES NOT STATE WHETHER AUGMENTED COPIES OF THE VALIDATION ORIGINALS WERE EXCLUDED FROM TRAINING, which is the question a reader of the 96.3% would want answered and it is an ABSENCE, not a stated flaw
senses.evidence: Different tests were performed with 2589 original images, when trained with 30880 images from database.

senses.label: `13 different types of plant diseases` - BOUNDED TO WHAT IS VISUALLY DIAGNOSABLE FROM A LEAF. The scope is set by what a photograph of a leaf can show, not by what matters agronomically, and the authors state that bound
senses.head: `13 different types of plant diseases`
senses.gloss: BOUNDED TO WHAT IS VISUALLY DIAGNOSABLE FROM A LEAF. The scope is set by what a photograph of a leaf can show, not by what matters agronomically, and the authors state that bound
senses.evidence: The developed model was able to detect leaf presence and distinguish between healthy leaves and 13 different diseases, which can be visually diagnosed.

senses.label: duplicate removal - BY METADATA ONLY: name, size and date, by script, then human assessment. Two copies of one photograph saved under different names and sizes would survive the automated pass, and the paper's guard against that is the expert review rather than image comparison
senses.head: duplicate removal
senses.gloss: BY METADATA ONLY: name, size and date, by script, then human assessment. Two copies of one photograph saved under different names and sizes would survive the automated pass, and the paper's guard against that is the expert review rather than image comparison
senses.evidence: In this stage, all duplicated images taken from different sources were removed by developed python script applying the comparing procedure. The script removed the duplicates by comparing the images’ metadata: name, size, and the date.

senses.label: the `comparison` - ONE SIDE IS MEASURED AND THE OTHER IS MODELLED, and the abstract says so in a clause easy to read past: conventional figures come from CROP BUDGETS AND GOVERNMENT STATISTICS, hydroponic figures are THEORETICAL DATA DERIVED BY ENGINEERING EQUATIONS POPULATED WITH LITERATURE VALUES. So `11x higher yields, 82x more energy` compares an observed system with a calculated one. Legitimate, and not what a reader assumes from the word `comparison` - every quantity on this record inherits it
senses.head: the `comparison`
senses.gloss: ONE SIDE IS MEASURED AND THE OTHER IS MODELLED, and the abstract says so in a clause easy to read past: conventional figures come from CROP BUDGETS AND GOVERNMENT STATISTICS, hydroponic figures are THEORETICAL DATA DERIVED BY ENGINEERING EQUATIONS POPULATED WITH LITERATURE VALUES. So `11x higher yields, 82x more energy` compares an observed system with a calculated one. Legitimate, and not what a reader assumes from the word `comparison` - every quantity on this record inherits it
senses.evidence: Data were obtained from crop budgets and governmental agricultural statistics, and contrasted with theoretical data for hydroponic lettuce production derived by using engineering equations populated with literature values.

senses.label: the hydroponic greenhouse - A SINGLE OPTIMISED HYPOTHETICAL, not a survey of installations: commercial scale, optimised for maximum production, one fixed size, sited in Yuma. The authors say hydroponic greenhouses `come in a variety of configurations and can be located almost anywhere` and that modelling several would be reasonable. The figures are therefore a best case at one site
senses.head: the hydroponic greenhouse
senses.gloss: A SINGLE OPTIMISED HYPOTHETICAL, not a survey of installations: commercial scale, optimised for maximum production, one fixed size, sited in Yuma. The authors say hydroponic greenhouses `come in a variety of configurations and can be located almost anywhere` and that modelling several would be reasonable. The figures are therefore a best case at one site
senses.evidence: Furthermore, as seen in Equation (2), the greenhouse was assumed to be of a specific size and located in Yuma, Arizona (one of the most productive areas for lettuce grown conventionally in the United States). In reality, hydroponic greenhouses come in a variety of configurations and can be located almost anywhere.

senses.label: `energy` here is DIRECT ENERGY ONLY - the study excludes energy embodied in chemical or material inputs, and excludes labour. The 82x ratio is a ratio of direct inputs, and the authors say a full life cycle assessment could produce alternative results
senses.head: `energy` here is DIRECT ENERGY ONLY
senses.gloss: the study excludes energy embodied in chemical or material inputs, and excludes labour. The 82x ratio is a ratio of direct inputs, and the authors say a full life cycle assessment could produce alternative results
senses.evidence: In addition, this study solely focused on direct energy inputs to hydroponic and conventional lettuce production and did not consider energy embodied in chemical or material inputs.

senses.label: `conventional agriculture` - DEFINED HISTORICALLY AND EXPLICITLY: growing crops in soil, in the open air, with irrigation and the active application of nutrients, pesticides and herbicides. A definition by PRACTICE rather than by yield or by certification, which is what makes the comparison well-posed
senses.head: `conventional agriculture`
senses.gloss: DEFINED HISTORICALLY AND EXPLICITLY: growing crops in soil, in the open air, with irrigation and the active application of nutrients, pesticides and herbicides. A definition by PRACTICE rather than by yield or by certification, which is what makes the comparison well-posed
senses.evidence: “Conventional” or “modern industrial agriculture” has been historically defined as the practice of growing crops in soil, in the open air, with irrigation, and the active application of nutrients, pesticides, and herbicides.

senses.label: symptoms of depression / anxiety / insomnia / distress, AS USED IN THE FOUR HEADLINE PREVALENCES - a count of everyone scoring above NORMAL on each scale, which is a far lower bar than the cutoff the same paper defines for detecting each disorder. Read this figure with the band boundaries tagged under definitions and with the two statistics rows that quote Table 2's own band counts; the number is right and the sense is milder than the words suggest
senses.head: symptoms of depression / anxiety / insomnia / distress, AS USED IN THE FOUR HEADLINE PREVALENCES
senses.gloss: a count of everyone scoring above NORMAL on each scale, which is a far lower bar than the cutoff the same paper defines for detecting each disorder. Read this figure with the band boundaries tagged under definitions and with the two statistics rows that quote Table 2's own band counts; the number is right and the sense is milder than the words suggest
senses.evidence: A considerable proportion of participants had symptoms of depression (634 \[50.4%\]), anxiety (560 \[44.6%\]), insomnia (427 \[34.0%\]), and distress (899 \[71.5%\]).

senses.label: severe symptoms - A SECOND AND HIGHER THRESHOLD IN THE SAME PAPER: a score greater than 10, 7, 15 or 26. For distress that cutoff of 26 falls at the boundary of the moderate band, while the 71.5% headline counts from the mild band up. SO `distress' IN THIS PAPER NAMES TWO DIFFERENT POPULATIONS DEPENDING ON WHICH SENTENCE YOU READ, and both are correct
senses.head: severe symptoms
senses.gloss: A SECOND AND HIGHER THRESHOLD IN THE SAME PAPER: a score greater than 10, 7, 15 or 26. For distress that cutoff of 26 falls at the boundary of the moderate band, while the 71.5% headline counts from the mild band up. SO `distress' IN THIS PAPER NAMES TWO DIFFERENT POPULATIONS DEPENDING ON WHICH SENTENCE YOU READ, and both are correct
senses.evidence: The cutoff score for detecting symptoms of major depression, anxiety, insomnia, and distress were 10, 7,14 15, and 26, respectively. Participants who had scores greater than the cutoff threshold were characterized as having severe symptoms.

senses.label: distress - A SCORE ON THE IMPACT OF EVENT SCALE-REVISED, an instrument for the psychological impact of a specific event, not a clinical diagnosis and not general unhappiness. The same instrument carries the same sense in wang2020, where the label is `psychological impact` instead
senses.head: distress
senses.gloss: A SCORE ON THE IMPACT OF EVENT SCALE-REVISED, an instrument for the psychological impact of a specific event, not a clinical diagnosis and not general unhappiness. The same instrument carries the same sense in wang2020, where the label is `psychological impact` instead
senses.evidence: Accordingly, the 9-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9; range, 0-27),10 the 7-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD-7) scale (range, 0-21),11 the 7-item Insomnia Severity Index (ISI; range, 0-28),12 and the 22-item Impact of Event Scale–Revised (IES-R; range, 0-88)13 were used to assess the severity of symptoms of depression, anxiety, insomnia, and distress, respectively.

senses.label: frontline - SELF-REPORTED AND BINARY. It is a yes/no answer to whether the respondent was directly engaged in diagnosing, treating or nursing patients with fever or confirmed COVID-19; it carries no measure of hours, caseload or duration of exposure
senses.head: frontline
senses.gloss: SELF-REPORTED AND BINARY. It is a yes/no answer to whether the respondent was directly engaged in diagnosing, treating or nursing patients with fever or confirmed COVID-19; it carries no measure of hours, caseload or duration of exposure
senses.evidence: Participants were asked whether they were directly engaged in clinical activities of diagnosing, treating, or providing nursing care to patients with elevated temperature or patients with confirmed COVID-19. Those who responded yes were defined as frontline workers, and those who answered no were defined as second-line workers.

senses.label: risk factor / associated with - AN ADJUSTED CROSS-SECTIONAL ODDS RATIO. Confounders are named and controlled, which is more than wang2020's univariate analysis does, but the design still observes no temporal order: nobody was measured before becoming frontline
senses.head: risk factor / associated with
senses.gloss: AN ADJUSTED CROSS-SECTIONAL ODDS RATIO. Confounders are named and controlled, which is more than wang2020's univariate analysis does, but the design still observes no temporal order: nobody was measured before becoming frontline
senses.evidence: To determine potential risk factors for symptoms of depression, anxiety, insomnia, and distress in participants, multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed, and the associations between risk factors and outcomes are presented as odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs, after adjustment for confounders, including sex, age, marital status, educational level, technical title, place of residence, working position (first-line or second-line), and type of hospital.

senses.label: weakly modeled - THE PAPER COINS THIS ABOUT ITSELF AND SAYS WHY. cWB is introduced as an unmodeled search, but the analysis reported here restricts it to signals that chirp in the time-frequency plane, so it is no longer model-free. The authors change the word rather than keep the stronger one
senses.head: weakly modeled
senses.gloss: THE PAPER COINS THIS ABOUT ITSELF AND SAYS WHY. cWB is introduced as an unmodeled search, but the analysis reported here restricts it to signals that chirp in the time-frequency plane, so it is no longer model-free. The authors change the word rather than keep the stronger one
senses.evidence: In contrast, the cWB search relies on no specific physical models of the source waveform, though in results presented here it does impose a restriction that signals are “chirping” in the time-frequency plane. We therefore refer to it as weakly modeled.

senses.label: marginal - NEITHER ESTABLISHED NOR EXCLUDED, and the paper holds that line to the end. A marginal trigger passed the false-alarm threshold but was given less than a 50% probability of astrophysical origin by both matched-filter searches. It is not a non-detection and not a weak detection: it is a candidate the collaboration declines to resolve, and it says so in the conclusions as well as the results
senses.head: marginal
senses.gloss: NEITHER ESTABLISHED NOR EXCLUDED, and the paper holds that line to the end. A marginal trigger passed the false-alarm threshold but was given less than a 50% probability of astrophysical origin by both matched-filter searches. It is not a non-detection and not a weak detection: it is a candidate the collaboration declines to resolve, and it says so in the conclusions as well as the results
senses.evidence: In addition, we list 14 GW candidate events that have an estimated false-alarm rate (FAR) less than 1 per 30 days in either of the two matched-filter analyses but whose astrophysical origin cannot be established nor excluded unambiguously (Sec. VII).

senses.label: false-alarm rate - AN EMPIRICAL RATE MEASURED AGAINST TIME-SHIFTED DATA, NOT A PROBABILITY THAT THE EVENT IS NOISE. Where a candidate outranks every background trigger the search can only report a BOUND, and the bound depends on how much background time was available - which is why some FARs here are larger than the ones previously published for the same events
senses.head: false-alarm rate
senses.gloss: AN EMPIRICAL RATE MEASURED AGAINST TIME-SHIFTED DATA, NOT A PROBABILITY THAT THE EVENT IS NOISE. Where a candidate outranks every background trigger the search can only report a BOUND, and the bound depends on how much background time was available - which is why some FARs here are larger than the ones previously published for the same events
senses.evidence: This restriction means, however, the minimum bound on the false-alarm rate of candidates that have a higher ranking statistic than any trigger in the background sample is larger than it would be if longer periods of data are used for the time-shift analysis.

senses.label: independent, of the three searches - INDEPENDENCE OF METHOD, NOT OF EVIDENCE. The conclusions say `three independent analyses` flatly; what is independent is the pipeline, the ranking statistic and the noise model, while the strain data are the same in all three. The body is more careful than the conclusion, which is worth knowing before the agreement between them is read as three confirmations
senses.head: independent, of the three searches
senses.gloss: INDEPENDENCE OF METHOD, NOT OF EVIDENCE. The conclusions say `three independent analyses` flatly; what is independent is the pipeline, the ranking statistic and the noise model, while the strain data are the same in all three. The body is more careful than the conclusion, which is worth knowing before the agreement between them is read as three confirmations
senses.evidence: The signals were discovered using three independent analyses: two matched-filter searches [8,9] and one weakly modeled burst search [11].

senses.label: GW versus marginal - A THRESHOLD CONVENTION, NOT A PROPERTY OF THE UNIVERSE. The boundary is a false-alarm rate ceiling of 1 per 30 days followed by a 50% astrophysical probability, both chosen by the collaboration. An event just under the line and one just over it differ by the convention, and the paper presents the choice as a choice
senses.head: GW versus marginal
senses.gloss: A THRESHOLD CONVENTION, NOT A PROPERTY OF THE UNIVERSE. The boundary is a false-alarm rate ceiling of 1 per 30 days followed by a 50% astrophysical probability, both chosen by the collaboration. An event just under the line and one just over it differ by the convention, and the paper presents the choice as a choice
senses.evidence: we assign the “GW” designation to any event for which the probability of astrophysical origin from either matched-filter search is greater than 50%

senses.label: detection, in the phrase `no new gravitational-wave events were discovered` - THE O1 REANALYSIS FOUND NOTHING NEW BUT DID CHANGE AN OLD ANSWER. The same data through better pipelines moved LVT151012 across the threshold and it is now GW151012. So the null result is about new events only; the catalog's contents still changed
senses.head: detection, in the phrase `no new gravitational-wave events were discovered`
senses.gloss: THE O1 REANALYSIS FOUND NOTHING NEW BUT DID CHANGE AN OLD ANSWER. The same data through better pipelines moved LVT151012 across the threshold and it is now GW151012. So the null result is about new events only; the catalog's contents still changed
senses.evidence: These improved FAR measurements for GW151012 are the most salient result of the reanalysis of O1 with the O2 pipelines; no new gravitational-wave events were discovered.

senses.label: sustainable agriculture - NOT DEFINED BY THIS PAPER. It is taken whole from Lehman et al., as a process that depletes no non-renewable resource essential to agriculture, and extended with Francis et al.'s `designing systems that close nutrient cycles`. Aquaponics then qualifies BY CONSTRUCTION, because closing a nutrient cycle is what it is. The definition is borrowed and the conclusion follows from the borrowing
senses.head: sustainable agriculture
senses.gloss: NOT DEFINED BY THIS PAPER. It is taken whole from Lehman et al., as a process that depletes no non-renewable resource essential to agriculture, and extended with Francis et al.'s `designing systems that close nutrient cycles`. Aquaponics then qualifies BY CONSTRUCTION, because closing a nutrient cycle is what it is. The definition is borrowed and the conclusion follows from the borrowing
senses.evidence: Aquaponics can be considered a sustainable agricultural production system regarding the definition of Lehman et al. \ [10\], who define sustainable agriculture as a process that does not deplete any non-renewable resources that are essential to agriculture in order to sustain the agricultural practices.

senses.label: nutrient concentration, when an aquaponic solution is compared with a hydroponic one - A MEASUREMENT, NOT A QUANTITY OF NUTRIENT. Electrical conductivity and aqueous filtration see only ions, and aquaponic dissolved solids include organic molecules with nutrients locked inside them. So the aquaponic column reads lower partly because the instrument cannot see what is there - and the authors print the comparison and this objection to it on the same page
senses.head: nutrient concentration, when an aquaponic solution is compared with a hydroponic one
senses.gloss: A MEASUREMENT, NOT A QUANTITY OF NUTRIENT. Electrical conductivity and aqueous filtration see only ions, and aquaponic dissolved solids include organic molecules with nutrients locked inside them. So the aquaponic column reads lower partly because the instrument cannot see what is there - and the authors print the comparison and this objection to it on the same page
senses.evidence: In hydroponics, TDS consists mainly of mineral compounds, while in aquaponics it includes organic molecules wherein nutrients can be locked up and overlooked by measuring procedures such as electrical conductivity (EC) or aqueous sample filtration. Both aqueous sample filtration and the EC measurement methods only take nutrients that are available in ionic form into account.

senses.label: challenge, the paper's own organising word - IT COVERS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND THE review does not separate them. Some challenges are engineering problems with candidate solutions (pH drift, and a lime-bed reactor to fix it). Others are ABSENCES IN THE LITERATURE - two economic studies, no comparison available, parameters unreported. A reader counting `challenges` counts both kinds together
senses.head: challenge, the paper's own organising word
senses.gloss: IT COVERS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND THE review does not separate them. Some challenges are engineering problems with candidate solutions (pH drift, and a lime-bed reactor to fix it). Others are ABSENCES IN THE LITERATURE - two economic studies, no comparison available, parameters unreported. A reader counting `challenges` counts both kinds together
senses.evidence: The current literature cannot be used to critically assess and predict economic challenges; as presented in Table 2, only two economic sub-studies are available in the peer-reviewed literature

senses.label: decoupled system - THE NAME FOR GIVING UP ON THE COMPROMISE. Fish, plants and nitrifying bacteria have different optimal pH and temperature, and a single loop must sit between them; a decoupled system runs two loops at their own optima and exchanges water periodically. It is presented as an alternative to the trade-off, not as an improvement to it
senses.head: decoupled system
senses.gloss: THE NAME FOR GIVING UP ON THE COMPROMISE. Fish, plants and nitrifying bacteria have different optimal pH and temperature, and a single loop must sit between them; a decoupled system runs two loops at their own optima and exchanges water periodically. It is presented as an alternative to the trade-off, not as an improvement to it
senses.evidence: the physical separation in two recirculating loops, i.e., an aquaculture and hydroponic loop, described as decoupled systems, where optimal condition for each system is applied with periodic water exchange between them.

senses.label: zero-discharge recirculating system - AN OBJECTIVE, NOT A DESCRIPTION. The paper says it `should be achievable` on Neori et al.'s authority and immediately says more research is needed on the solubilization it depends on. Nothing in the review reports one running
senses.head: zero-discharge recirculating system
senses.gloss: AN OBJECTIVE, NOT A DESCRIPTION. The paper says it `should be achievable` on Neori et al.'s authority and immediately says more research is needed on the solubilization it depends on. Nothing in the review reports one running
senses.evidence: Given the objective of obtaining a low environmental footprint, a zero-discharge recirculating system concept should be achievable according to Neori et al. \ [52\], but more research needs to be carried out on fish waste solubilization with the objective to transform all added nutrients into plant biomass.

senses.label: COVID-19 impact indicator - THE PAPER PRE-EMPTS ITS OWN MISREADING AND SAYS SO OUTRIGHT: human mobility and infection rate `should not be interpreted as risk factors`. They are PROXIES for the pandemic, which is the risk factor. GBD 2020 does this by estimating prevalence across a cascade down five levels of a geographical hierarchy: global, super-region, region, country or territory, and subnational locations. The prevalence from locations higher in the hierarchy act as priors for the prevalence for locations lower in the hierarchy.

senses.label: GEPIA2 - enhanced GEPIA with transcript-level, subtype-level, uploaded-data, and batch-API analysis
senses.head: GEPIA2
senses.gloss: enhanced GEPIA with transcript-level, subtype-level, uploaded-data, and batch-API analysis
senses.evidence: Introduced in 2017, the GEPIA (Gene Expression Profiling Interactive Analysis) web server has been a valuable and highly cited resource for gene expression analysis based on tumor and normal samples from the TCGA and the GTEx databases. Here, we present GEPIA2, an updated and enhanced version to provide insights with higher resolution and more functionalities. Featuring 198 619 isoforms and 84 cancer subtypes, GEPIA2 has extended gene expression quantification from the gene level to the transcript level, and supports analysis of a specific cancer subtype, and comparison between subtypes. In addition, GEPIA2 has adopted new analysis techniques of gene signature quantification inspired by single-cell sequencing studies, and provides customized analysis where users can upload their own RNA-seq data and compare them with TCGA and GTEx samples. We also offer an API for batch process and easy retrieval of the analysis results

senses.label: Resolution shift - expression quantification moves from gene level to individual transcripts and cancer subtypes
senses.head: Resolution shift
senses.gloss: expression quantification moves from gene level to individual transcripts and cancer subtypes
senses.evidence: Introduced in 2017, the GEPIA (Gene Expression Profiling Interactive Analysis) web server has been a valuable and highly cited resource for gene expression analysis based on tumor and normal samples from the TCGA and the GTEx databases. Here, we present GEPIA2, an updated and enhanced version to provide insights with higher resolution and more functionalities. Featuring 198 619 isoforms and 84 cancer subtypes, GEPIA2 has extended gene expression quantification from the gene level to the transcript level, and supports analysis of a specific cancer subtype, and comparison between subtypes. In addition, GEPIA2 has adopted new analysis techniques of gene signature quantification inspired by single-cell sequencing studies, and provides customized analysis where users can upload their own RNA-seq data and compare them with TCGA and GTEx samples. We also offer an API for batch process and easy retrieval of the analysis results

senses.label: Survival analysis - links expression level to prognostic outcome to assess clinical relevance
senses.head: Survival analysis
senses.gloss: links expression level to prognostic outcome to assess clinical relevance
senses.evidence: Valuable cancer-related RNA sequencing resources like TCGA and GTEx have provided ample opportunities for data mining and deeper understanding of gene functions. As these data became available to researchers, numerous methods and procedures for analyzing large gene expression datasets also emerged, some of which were later accepted as common practices for mining such data. Survival analysis, for example, allows the identification of links between gene expression levels and prognostic outcomes, and hence has been widely used for evaluating the clinical relevance of a given gene. To facilitate the intuitive and interactive application of such methods to the TCGA and the GTEx datasets, we initially developed the GEPIA web server in 2016. Armed with functionalities such as differential expression analysis, survival analysis, and similar gene identification, GEPIA provided experimental biologists and clinicians with a handy tool to explore TCGA and GTEx datasets. GEPIA has aided the investigation of various genes in multiple cancer types, and led to the identification of potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets

senses.label: Gene signature - curated gene set used to interrogate tumor-microenvironment composition or infiltrating-immune functional state
senses.head: Gene signature
senses.gloss: curated gene set used to interrogate tumor-microenvironment composition or infiltrating-immune functional state
senses.evidence: As we continuously accommodate the feedbacks and requests from our users, we have identified new angles to explore the TCGA and GTEx resources, and have thus developed a much-enhanced new version of GEPIA, named GEPIA2. For example, alternative splicing, resulting in different isoform usages, has gained traction in cancer target finding. In GEPIA2, we utilized the UCSC Xena recomputed data of TCGA and GTEx for 198,619 coding and a series of other non-coding transcripts, and developed new computational functionalities to explore such events. Additionally, cancers are often comprised by heterogeneous subtypes with distinct prognosis. For instance, MSI and MSS colorectal cancers respond differently to chemotherapy and immunotherapy. To better investigate the underlying biological mechanisms of different cancer subtypes, GEPIA2 allows users to fine-tune their analyses to focus on each of the 84 cancer subtypes, and to compare across different subtypes. Furthermore, with single-cell sequencing becoming widely available, new paradigms of analysis have surfaced. In particular, gene signatures are often used to interrogate the composition of tumor microenvironment and the functional status of infiltrating immune content. Such techniques are also integrated in to GEPIA2 as we provide signature-based functionalities with a curated list of signatures for efficient investigation. Finally, GEPIA2 provides features to process user-uploaded expression data and compare such data with the large collection of TCGA and GTEx samples

senses.label: Survival map - context-sensitive gene or isoform prognosis summarized across selected cancer types
senses.head: Survival map
senses.gloss: context-sensitive gene or isoform prognosis summarized across selected cancer types
senses.evidence: GEPIA2 performs survival analyses based on gene or isoform expression levels. Given a list of custom cancer types, GEPIA2 would provide a heat map to show the survival analysis result based on multiple cancer types (Figure 2A). The red blocks denote higher and blue ones lower risk, with an increase in the gene or isoform expression. The blocks with darkened frames indicate statistical significance in prognostic analyses. Since gene survival analyses can be context-dependent, this function allows users to screen for the prognostic impact of a gene or an isoform across different cancer types

senses.label: Uploaded expression comparison - normalize a user matrix with a public target and return differential expression as a boxplot
senses.head: Uploaded expression comparison
senses.gloss: normalize a user matrix with a public target and return differential expression as a boxplot
senses.evidence: GEPIA2 bridges the gap between users’ custom data and the public cancer genomic data. This function enables users to upload their own data for performing differential analysis with the tumor or normal data from TCGA or GTEx projects. After the Quantile-normalization or other two additional normalization strategies (inspired by GenomeSpace) based on the uploaded dataset and the target dataset on the server, GEPIA2 performs the differential expression analysis and return result in boxplot

senses.label: Classifier modes - known cancer type gives sensitive subtype prediction; unrestricted mode addresses unknown origin
senses.head: Classifier modes
senses.gloss: known cancer type gives sensitive subtype prediction; unrestricted mode addresses unknown origin
senses.evidence: With this function, users can accurately predict the cancer type or cancer-subtype of their uploaded samples based on the gene expression. The classifier is trained by TCGA expression data. For each sample, the probability of this sample belonging to each subtype would be listed below. We provide two modes to work with the classifier by choosing the actual cancer type first and predict for its corresponding subtypes or directly predict with the range of all cancer subtypes. The former way provides a more sensitive result, and the latter will be more useful for the identification of the cancer with unknown origin

senses.label: Isoform analysis - profile expression, differential status, prognosis, and pairwise correlation using transcript identifiers
senses.head: Isoform analysis
senses.gloss: profile expression, differential status, prognosis, and pairwise correlation using transcript identifiers
senses.evidence: Except for multiple gene comparison and dimensionality reduction functions, GEPIA2 allows users to perform all expression analyses at the isoform level (Table 1). Users can input an isoform symbol (e.g. ERBB2–001) or an Ensembl ID (e.g. ENST00000584601) to analyze an isoform of interest. Using different features, users can profile the isoform expression across different cancer types, obtain the differentially expressed isoforms, discover the prognostic isoforms and examine the correlation between two isoforms. Meanwhile, analyses based on both the gene and isoform levels could be performed to reveal the similarities or differences between them

senses.label: Python API - batch requests and streamlined retrieval for five analysis functions
senses.head: Python API
senses.gloss: batch requests and streamlined retrieval for five analysis functions
senses.evidence: GEPIA2 python API provides users with access to GEPIA2’s analyses from a programming environment. Designed to perform multiple requests for our service, it boosts the efficiency of users by allowing batch process and streamlining results retrieval. The API is implemented in python language and we provide a tutorial for users to utilize the API. The python package provides access to 5 functionalities: boxplot, similar, correlation, survival and survival map

senses.label: layer-wise relevance propagation = whatever satisfies the constraints; several different algorithms qualify
senses.evidence: It is important to note that the definition is not given as an algorithm or a solution of an objective with a distinct minimum. Instead, it is given as a set of constraints that the solution should satisfy. Thus, different algorithms with different resulting solutions may be admissible under these constraints.

senses.label: HEA = typically five or more elements in equimolar concentration, giving maximum molar configurational entropy RlnN
senses.evidence: In an HEA, the configurational entropy of a solid-solution phase is maximized to stabilize it against the formation of intermetallics. Typically, five or more elements can be mixed in a HEA in equimolar concentrations to produce a maximum molar configurational entropy of ΔSmix = RlnN, where N is the number of equimolar components and R is the gas constant.

senses.label: 'high-entropy material' HAS A CONTESTED SCOPE - glasses count only 'in a broad definition', said in parentheses
senses.head: 'high-entropy material' HAS A CONTESTED SCOPE
senses.gloss: glasses count only 'in a broad definition', said in parentheses
senses.evidence: Most prior studies of crystalline high-entropy materials have been conducted for metallic HEAs of mostly simple face- and body-centered cubic (FCC and BCC), as well as occasionally hexagonal close packing (HCP), crystal structures; much less studies have been done for making crystalline high-entropy ceramics (albeit that glasses can be considered high-entropy materials in a broad definition), particularly those with more complex, non-cubic, crystal structures.

senses.label: delta <= 4% or 4.3% = a NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT criterion, and it is empirical, not derived
senses.evidence: Prior studies suggested, mostly based on empirical observations, that a necessary (but not sufficient) criterion for forming a single-phase (disordered) HEA is that the computed δ of the solid solution should be sufficiently small: δ ≤ δmax ≈ 4% or 4.3%.

senses.label: the same delta, recomputed from LATTICE CONSTANTS instead of atomic radii, because no radius represents the real bond lengths
senses.evidence: In reality, metal diborides [M2+(B−)2] form a highly anisotropic layered structure (i.e., the hexagonal AlB2 structure), where each metal atom donates two electrons and the M-B bonds (between the metal and B layers) have mixed ionic and covalent characteristics (see Fig. 1). Within the 2D metal layers, M-M bonds are strained significantly by the more rigid boron net (Fig. 1). Thus, none of the available (metallic, covalent or ionic) radii can effectively represent the actual bond lengths in the metal diborides in the AlB2 structure (Fig. 1).

senses.label: 'only one necessary, but not essential, condition' - the authors' own hedge on their replacement
senses.head: 'only one necessary, but not essential, condition'
senses.gloss: the authors' own hedge on their replacement

A very small δ value is certainly not a guarantee for forming a single-phase, high-entropy, solid solution.

senses.label: delta-c is the discriminating one and delta-a is not, because the boron net constrains the a-axis
senses.evidence: Interestingly, the computed δa values are small (in the range of 1.3% to 2.3% for all seven specimens) because the M-M bonds are strained by the rigid boron net (that can deform metal cations and M-M bond lengths towards an ideal “strain-free” value dictated by stronger B-B bonds; Fig. 1). senses.label: GNoME discovery flywheel - generate candidates, filter with GNNs, verify energies with DFT, and reuse results as next-round training data
senses.head: GNoME discovery flywheel
senses.gloss: generate candidates, filter with GNNs, verify energies with DFT, and reuse results as next-round training data
senses.evidence: In this paper, we scale up machine learning for materials exploration through large-scale active learning, yielding the first models that accurately predict stability and, therefore, can guide materials discovery. Our approach relies on two pillars: first, we establish methods for generating diverse candidate structures, including new symmetry-aware partial substitutions (SAPS) and random structure search. Second, we use state-of-the art graph neural networks (GNNs) that improve modelling of material properties given structure or composition. In a series of rounds, these graph networks for materials exploration (GNoME) are trained on available data and used to filter candidate structures. The energy of the filtered candidates is computed using DFT, both verifying model predictions and serving as a data flywheel to train more robust models on larger datasets in the next round of active learning

senses.label: Structural framework - modify known crystals, expand substitutions with SAPS, quantify uncertainty, cluster polymorphs, and rank for DFT
senses.head: Structural framework
senses.gloss: modify known crystals, expand substitutions with SAPS, quantify uncertainty, cluster polymorphs, and rank for DFT
senses.evidence: To generate and filter candidates, we use two frameworks, which are visualized in Fig. 1a. First, structural candidates are generated by modifications of available crystals. However, we strongly augment the set of substitutions by adjusting ionic substitution probabilities to give priority to discovery and use newly proposed symmetry aware partial substitutions (SAPS) to efficiently enable incomplete replacements. This expansion results in more than 109 candidates over the course of active learning; the resulting structures are filtered by means of GNoME using volume-based test-time augmentation and uncertainty quantification through deep ensembles. Finally, structures are clustered and polymorphs are ranked for evaluation with DFT (see Methods). In the second framework, compositional models predict stability without structural information. Inputs are reduced chemical formulas. Generation by means of oxidation-state balancing is often too strict (for example, neglecting Li15Si4). Using relaxed constraints (see Methods), we filter compositions using GNoME and initialize 100 random structures for evaluation through ab initio random structure searching (AIRSS). In both frameworks, models provide a prediction of energy and a threshold is chosen on the basis of the relative stability (decomposition energy) with respect to competing phases. Evaluation is performed through DFT computations in the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP) and we measure both the number of stable materials discovered as well as the precision of predicted stable materials (hit rate) in comparison with the Materials Project

senses.label: Compositional framework - predict from reduced formulas, relax oxidation constraints, filter compositions, and initialize AIRSS structures
senses.head: Compositional framework
senses.gloss: predict from reduced formulas, relax oxidation constraints, filter compositions, and initialize AIRSS structures
senses.evidence: To generate and filter candidates, we use two frameworks, which are visualized in Fig. 1a. First, structural candidates are generated by modifications of available crystals. However, we strongly augment the set of substitutions by adjusting ionic substitution probabilities to give priority to discovery and use newly proposed symmetry aware partial substitutions (SAPS) to efficiently enable incomplete replacements. This expansion results in more than 109 candidates over the course of active learning; the resulting structures are filtered by means of GNoME using volume-based test-time augmentation and uncertainty quantification through deep ensembles. Finally, structures are clustered and polymorphs are ranked for evaluation with DFT (see Methods). In the second framework, compositional models predict stability without structural information. Inputs are reduced chemical formulas. Generation by means of oxidation-state balancing is often too strict (for example, neglecting Li15Si4). Using relaxed constraints (see Methods), we filter compositions using GNoME and initialize 100 random structures for evaluation through ab initio random structure searching (AIRSS). In both frameworks, models provide a prediction of energy and a threshold is chosen on the basis of the relative stability (decomposition energy) with respect to competing phases. Evaluation is performed through DFT computations in the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP) and we measure both the number of stable materials discovered as well as the precision of predicted stable materials (hit rate) in comparison with the Materials Project

senses.label: GNoME graph model - element embeddings and message passing predict total crystal energy
senses.head: GNoME graph model
senses.gloss: element embeddings and message passing predict total crystal energy
senses.evidence: All GNoME models are GNNs that predict the total energy of a crystal. Inputs are converted to a graph through a one-hot embedding of the elements. We follow the message-passing formulation, in which aggregate projections are shallow multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) with swish nonlinearities. For structural models, we find it important to normalize messages from edges to nodes by the average adjacency of atoms across the entire dataset. Initial models are trained on a snapshot of the Materials Project from 2018 of approximately 69,000 materials. Previous work benchmarked this task at a mean absolute error (MAE) of 28 meV atom−1 (ref. ); however, we find that the improved networks achieve a MAE of 21 meV atom−1. We fix this promising architecture (see Methods) and focus on scaling in the rest of this paper

senses.label: Scaling law - GNoME test loss improves by a power law as training data increase
senses.head: Scaling law
senses.gloss: GNoME test loss improves by a power law as training data increase
senses.evidence: The test loss performance of GNoME models exhibit improvement as a power law with further data. These results are in line with neural scaling laws in deep learning and suggest that further discovery efforts could continue to improve generalization. Emphatically, unlike the case of language or vision, in materials science, we can continue to generate data and discover stable crystals, which can be reused to continue scaling up the model. We also demonstrate emergent generalization to out-of-distribution tasks by testing structural models trained on data originating from substitutions on crystals arising from random search in Fig. 1e. These examples are often high-energy local minima and out of distribution compared with data generated by our structural pipeline (which, by virtue of substitutions, contains structures near their minima). Nonetheless, we observe clear improvement with scale. These results indicate that final GNoME models are a substantial step towards providing the community with a universal energy predictor, capable of handling diverse materials structures through deep learning

Emphatically, unlike the case of language or vision, in materials science, we can continue to generate data and discover stable crystals, which can be reused to continue scaling up the model. We also demonstrate emergent generalization to out-of-distribution tasks by testing structural models trained on data originating from substitutions on crystals arising from random search in Fig. 1e. These examples are often high-energy local minima and out of distribution compared with data generated by our structural pipeline (which, by virtue of substitutions, contains structures near their minima). senses.label: General-purpose MLIP - potential pretrained on diverse ionic-relaxation energies and forces for zero-shot bulk-solid use
senses.head: General-purpose MLIP
senses.gloss: potential pretrained on diverse ionic-relaxation energies and forces for zero-shot bulk-solid use
senses.evidence: The process of discovery of stable crystals also provides a data source beyond stable materials. In particular, the ionic relaxations involve computation of first-principles energies and forces for a diverse set of materials structures. This generates a dataset of unprecedented diversity and scale, which we explore to pretrain a general-purpose machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) for bulk solids. MLIPs have become a promising tool to accelerate the simulation of materials by learning the energies and forces of reference structures computed at first-principles accuracy. Existing efforts typically train models per material, with data often sampled from ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD). This markedly limits their general applicability and adoption, requiring expensive data collection and training a new potential from scratch for each system. By making use of the GNoME dataset of first-principles calculations from diverse structural relaxations, we demonstrate that large-scale pretraining of MLIPs enables models that show unprecedented zero-shot accuracy and can be used to discover superionic conductors, without training on any material-specific data

senses.label: Zero-shot evaluation - pretrained potential applied to unseen compositions, melted structures, vacancies, and AIMD data without AIMD training
senses.head: Zero-shot evaluation
senses.gloss: pretrained potential applied to unseen compositions, melted structures, vacancies, and AIMD data without AIMD training
senses.evidence: We scale pretraining of a NequIP potential on data sampled from ionic relaxations. Increasing the pretraining dataset, we observe consistent power-law improvements in accuracy (see Fig. 3a,b). Despite only being trained on ionic relaxations and not on molecular-dynamics data, the pretrained GNoME potential shows remarkable accuracy when evaluated on downstream data sampled from the new distribution of AIMD in a zero-shot manner, that is, in which no training data originate from AIMD simulations (see Fig. 3). Notably, this includes unseen compositions, melted structures and structures including vacancies, all of which are not included in our training set (see Supplementary Note 6.4). In particular, we find that the scale of the GNoME dataset allows it to outperform existing general-purpose potentials (see Fig. 3d) and makes the pretrained potential competitive with models trained explicitly on hundreds of samples from the target data distributions (see Supplementary Note 6.4). We observe particularly pronounced improvements in the transferability of MLIPs, one of the most pressing shortcomings of MLIPs. To assess the transferability of the potentials, we test their performance under distribution shift: we train two types of NequIP potential on structures sampled from AIMD at T = 400 K, one in which the network is trained from randomly initialized weights and the other in which we fine-tune from a pretrained GNoME checkpoint. We then measure the performance of both potentials on data sampled from AIMD at T = 1,000 K (see Fig. 3c), out of distribution with respective to the 400-K data. The potential pretrained on GNoME data shows systematic and strong improvements in transferability over the potential trained from scratch, even when training is performed on more than 1,000 structures. The zero-shot GNoME potential, not fine-tuned on any data from this composition, outperforms even a state-of-the-art NequIP model trained on hundreds of structures

senses.label: 'fear of COVID-19' = the SEVEN ITEMS that survived 30 measures, two expert panels and one correlation cutoff
senses.evidence: First, an extensive literature review was conducted to assess all general scales on fear. Thirty measures on fear were identified that assess fear on different populations and diseases (available on request from the corresponding authors). Relevant and possible items were pooled by two researchers (i.e., the third and last authors). After removing those items with similar content or expressions, 28 items were retained for further evaluation. Second, an expert panel (comprising a psychologist, virologist, health psychologist, psychiatrist, general physician, and nurse) evaluated the 28 items, and 11 items were deleted based on the suggestion from the expert panel. Third, the retained 17 items were sent out to a different expert panel (comprising a health education specialist, pulmonologist, social psychologist, and sociologist in Iran) to review. Seven items were further omitted based on the comments from the second expert panel.

senses.label: the last three items were removed for corrected item-total correlations of -0.06, -0.03 and -0.05 - a criterion INTERNAL to the instrument
senses.head: the last three items were removed for corrected item-total correlations of -0.06, -0.03 and -0.05
senses.gloss: a criterion INTERNAL to the instrument
senses.evidence: According to the corrected inter-item correlation, three items with low corrected item-total correlations were deleted (i.e., Item 3, − 0.06; Item 4, − 0.03; Item 5 − 0.05). The remaining seven items in the scale all had acceptable corrected item-total correlation (0.47 to 0.56) and were used for following psychometric testing (Table 1).

senses.label: a higher total score MEANS more severe fear - the interpretation is stipulated, not derived
senses.head: a higher total score MEANS more severe fear
senses.gloss: the interpretation is stipulated, not derived
senses.evidence: Moreover, the overall score of the summed-up items scores can indicate the severity of the fear of COVID-19. More specifically, the higher the score on the FCV-19S, the higher the scores on the HADS and the PVDS were. Therefore, higher overall scores on the FCV-19S indicate more severe fear of COVID-19.

senses.label: scoring = seven items, 1 to 5 each, summed to a range of 7 to 35
senses.evidence: The participants indicate their level of agreement with the statements using a five-item Likert-type scale. Answers included “strongly disagree,” “disagree,” “neither agree nor disagree,” “agree,” and “strongly agree”. The minimum score possible for each question is 1, and the maximum is 5. A total score is calculated by adding up each item score (ranging from 7 to 35). The higher the score, the greater the fear of cororonavirus-19.

senses.label: 'valid' here = correlating with the HADS and the PVDS; there is no external criterion for fear
senses.evidence: Also, the FCV-19S significantly correlated with depression, anxiety (on the HADS), perceived infectability, and germ aversion (on the PVDS) which suggests that individuals with severe fear of COVID-19 may have these comorbid disorders.

senses.head: a NON-DETECT is entered as LOD divided by the square root of 2

senses.evidence: For concentrations below the LOD, as recommended for the analysis of NHANES data, we used a value equal to the LOD divided by the square root of 2.

senses.head: a SMOKER is anyone with serum cotinine above 10 ug/L

senses.evidence: Participants were categorized as smokers if their serum cotinine concentrations were > 10 μg/L.
